translations.literal: Kong Shao'an; Zi Zhen; Ji Xu; Sun Ruosi; Yuan Lang; younger paternal cousin Chengxu; younger paternal cousin of the same grandfather Li Zhen; Sun Yi; He Deren; Yu Bao; Cai Yungong; Zheng Shiyi; Xie Yan; Cui Xinming; son Dongri; Zhang Yungu; Liu Yinshi; nephew Yanyou; son of elder paternal cousin Zangqi; Zhang Changling; elder brother Changzong; Cui Xinggong; Meng Lizhen; elder brother Yongzhong; Dong Sigong; Yuan Sijing; Xu Qipan; Du Yijian; younger paternal cousin of the same grandfather Shenyan; Lu Zhaolin; elder brother Guangcheng; Yang Jiong; younger paternal uncle Degan; Degan's son Shenrang; Wang Bo; Luo Binwang; Deng Xuanting.

sentences.zh: 臣觀前代秉筆論文者多矣。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that those of former ages who took up the brush to discuss literature were many.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject observes that in former ages many men took up the brush to discuss literature.

sentences.zh: 莫不憲章《謨》、《誥》，祖述《詩》、《騷》；

translations.literal: None failed to take the Documents of Yu and the Announcements as their model, or to trace their lineage to the Classic of Poetry and the Songs of Chu;
translations.idiomatic: All took the Documents of Yu and the Announcements as their model and traced their lineage to the Classic of Poetry and the Songs of Chu;

sentences.zh: 遠宗毛、鄭之訓論，近鄙班、揚之述作。

translations.literal: in the distant past they revered the commentaries of Mao and Zheng, while in recent times they disdained the compositions of Ban and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: in distant antiquity they revered the commentaries of Mao and Zheng, while in recent times they disdained the compositions of Ban and Yang.

sentences.zh: 謂「采采苤諲」，獨高比興之源；

translations.literal: They held that "Plucking the water-chestnut," alone towers as the source of allegory and evocation;
translations.idiomatic: They held that "Plucking the water-chestnut" alone towers as the source of allegory and evocation;

sentences.zh: 「湛湛江楓」，長擅詠歌之體。

translations.literal: "Deep, deep the river maples," excels long in the form of lyric song.
translations.idiomatic: "Deep, deep the river maples" excels in the form of lyric song.

sentences.zh: 殊不知世代有文質，風俗有淳醨；

translations.literal: They little knew that generations differ in refinement and plainness, and customs in purity and decadence;
translations.idiomatic: They little knew that generations differ in refinement and plainness, and that customs differ in purity and decadence;

sentences.zh: 學識有淺深，才性有工拙。

translations.literal: learning and knowledge differ in depth and shallowness, and talent and nature in skill and clumsiness.
translations.idiomatic: that learning and knowledge differ in depth and shallowness, and talent and nature in skill and clumsiness.

sentences.zh: 昔仲尼演三代之《易》，刪諸國之《詩》，非求勝於昔賢，要取名於今代。

translations.literal: Formerly Confucius elaborated the Changes of the Three Dynasties and culled the poems of the various states—not to surpass the sages of old, but to win a name in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Confucius elaborated the Changes of the Three Dynasties and culled the poems of the various states—not to surpass the sages of old, but to win a name in the present age.

sentences.zh: 實以淳樸之時傷質，民俗之語不經，故飾以文言，考之弦誦。

translations.literal: In truth, in an age of plain simplicity he lamented crudity, and the speech of common folk was unpolished; therefore he adorned it with literary language and set it to recitation on the strings.
translations.idiomatic: In truth, in an age of plain simplicity he lamented crudity, and the speech of common folk was unpolished; therefore he adorned it with literary language and set it to recitation on the strings.

sentences.zh: 然後致遠不泥，永代作程，即知是古非今，未為通論。

translations.literal: Only then did it reach far without sticking fast, and serve as a standard for all time—thus one knows that to exalt antiquity and reject the present is no comprehensive judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did it reach far without sticking fast and serve as a standard for all time—thus one knows that to exalt antiquity and reject the present is no comprehensive judgment.

sentences.zh: 夫執鑒寫形，持衡品物，非伯樂不能分駑驥之狀，非延陵不能別《雅》、《鄭》之音。

translations.literal: To hold a mirror and draw a likeness, to hold a balance and appraise things—without Bo Le one cannot distinguish the forms of nags and thoroughbreds; without Yanling one cannot tell apart the tones of the Elegant and the Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: To hold a mirror and draw a likeness, to hold a balance and appraise things—without Bo Le one cannot distinguish nags from thoroughbreds; without Yanling one cannot tell apart the tones of the Elegant and the Zheng.

sentences.zh: 若空混吹竽之人，即異聞《韶》之嘆。

translations.literal: If one merely mixes in those who blow on the yu without knowing how, one differs from those who heard the Shao and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: If one merely mixes in those who blow on the yu without knowing how, one differs from those who heard the Shao and sighed.

sentences.zh: 近代唯沈隱俟斟酌《二南》，剖陳三變；

translations.literal: In recent times only Shen Yue weighed the Two Souths and analyzed the three transformations;
translations.idiomatic: In recent times only Shen Yue weighed the Two Souths and analyzed the three transformations;

sentences.zh: 攄雲、淵之抑郁，振潘、陸之風徽。

translations.literal: he gave voice to the melancholy of Bao and Yuan, and revived the fine style of Pan and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: he gave voice to the melancholy of Bao and Yuan and revived the fine style of Pan and Lu.

sentences.zh: 俾律呂和諧，宮商輯洽，不獨子建總建安之霸，客兒擅江左之雄。

translations.literal: He made pitch and mode harmonious and palace and merchant tones accord—not only did Zijian gather the hegemony of the Jian'an era, and Keren monopolize the glory of the Jiangzuo.
translations.idiomatic: He made pitch and mode harmonious and palace and merchant tones accord—not only did Zijian gather the hegemony of the Jian'an era and Keren monopolize the glory of the Jiangzuo.

sentences.zh: 爰及我朝，挺生賢俊，文皇帝解戎衣而開學校，飾賁帛而禮儒生；

translations.literal: Down to our dynasty, worthy and brilliant men arose; the Literary Emperor laid aside armor and opened schools, adorned silks and honored Confucian scholars;
translations.idiomatic: Down to our dynasty worthy and brilliant men arose; the Literary Emperor laid aside armor and opened schools, adorned silks and honored Confucian scholars;

sentences.zh: 門羅吐鳳之才，人擅握蛇之價。

translations.literal: his gates gathered talents that could make the phoenix speak, and every man possessed the worth of one who grasped the snake.
translations.idiomatic: his gates gathered talents that could make the phoenix speak, and every man possessed the worth of one who grasped the snake.

sentences.zh: 靡不發言為論，下筆成文，足以緯俗經邦，豈止雕章縟句。

translations.literal: None failed to speak and become discourse, or take up the brush and complete a composition—enough to bind custom and govern the state, not merely to carve chapters and weave sentences.
translations.idiomatic: None failed to speak and become discourse or take up the brush and complete a composition—enough to bind custom and govern the state, not merely to carve chapters and weave sentences.

sentences.zh: 韻諧金奏，詞炳丹青，故貞觀之風，同乎三代。

translations.literal: Rhyme harmonized with golden music, words blazed like cinnabar and azure; therefore the style of the Zhenguan era matched the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Rhyme harmonized with golden music and words blazed like cinnabar and azure; therefore the style of the Zhenguan era matched the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 高宗、天後，尤重詳延；

translations.literal: Under Gaozong and the Heavenly Empress, court patronage was especially broad and detailed;
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong and the Heavenly Empress, court patronage was especially broad and detailed;

sentences.zh: 天子賦橫汾之詩，臣下繼柏梁之奏；

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven composed the poem on crossing the Fen, and his ministers followed with the Bo Liang ode;
translations.idiomatic: the Son of Heaven composed the poem on crossing the Fen, and his ministers followed with the Bo Liang ode;

sentences.zh: 巍巍濟濟，輝爍古今。

translations.literal: towering and abundant, they shine through past and present.
translations.idiomatic: towering and abundant, they shine through past and present.

sentences.zh: 如燕、許之潤色王言，吳、陸之鋪揚鴻業，元稹、劉蕡之對策，王維、杜甫之雕蟲，並非肄業使然，自是天機秀絕。

translations.literal: Such as Yan and Xu polishing the royal words, Wu and Lu spreading the great enterprise, Yuan Zhen and Liu Zao answering policy questions, Wang Wei and Du Fu carving fine phrases—all were not merely so because of training, but by nature possessed supreme genius.
translations.idiomatic: Such as Yan and Xu polishing the royal words, Wu and Lu spreading the great enterprise, Yuan Zhan and Liu Zao answering policy questions, Wang Wei and Du Fu carving fine phrases—all were not merely so because of training, but by nature possessed supreme genius.

sentences.zh: 若隋珠色澤，無假淬磨，孔璣翠羽，自成華彩，置之文苑，實煥緗圖。

translations.literal: Like the luster of Sui pearls, needing no tempering by grindstone; like the emerald feathers of Kong feathers, forming their own splendor—placed in the grove of letters, they truly brighten the silk scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Like the luster of Sui pearls, needing no tempering by grindstone; like the emerald feathers of Kong feathers, forming their own splendor—placed in the grove of letters, they truly brighten the silk scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其間爵位崇高，別為之傳。

translations.literal: Among them those of lofty rank and eminence are given separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Among them those of lofty rank and eminence are given separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 今采孔紹安已下，為《文苑》三篇，凱懷才憔悴之徒，千古見知於作者。

translations.literal: Now I gather from Kong Shao'an downward into three chapters of Men of Letters, cherishing those of talent who withered in obscurity, that through the ages they may be known to authors.
translations.idiomatic: Now I gather from Kong Shao'an downward into three chapters of Men of Letters, cherishing those of talent who withered in obscurity, that through the ages they may be known to authors.

sentences.zh: 孔紹安

translations.literal: Kong Shao'an
translations.idiomatic: Kong Shao'an

sentences.zh: 孔紹安，越州山陰人，陳吏部尚書奐之子。

translations.literal: Kong Shao'an was a man of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture, son of Huan, Minister of the Civil Service of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Shao'an was a man of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture, son of Huan, Minister of the Civil Service of Chen.

sentences.zh: 少與兄紹新，俱以文詞知名。

translations.literal: In youth he and his elder brother Shaoxin were both renowned for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and his elder brother Shaoxin were both renowned for literary composition.

sentences.zh: 十三，陳亡入隋，徙居京兆鄠縣。

translations.literal: At thirteen, when Chen fell and he entered Sui, he moved to Hu County in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, when Chen fell and he entered Sui, he moved to Hu County in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 閉門讀書，誦古文集數十萬言，外兄虞世南嘆異之。

translations.literal: He shut his doors and read books, reciting several hundred thousand words of ancient collected writings; his maternal cousin Yu Shinan marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his doors and read books, reciting several hundred thousand words of ancient collected writings; his maternal cousin Yu Shinan marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 紹新嘗謂世南曰：「本朝淪陷，分從湮滅，但見此弟，竊謂家族不亡矣！」

translations.literal: Shaoxin once said to Shinan: "Our dynasty has fallen and been scattered and extinguished, but seeing this younger brother, I secretly say the clan is not dead!"
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxin once said to Shinan, "Our dynasty has fallen and been scattered and extinguished, but seeing this younger brother, I secretly say the clan is not dead!"

sentences.zh: 時有詞人孫萬壽，與紹安篤忘年之好，時人稱為孫、孔。

translations.literal: At the time the writer Sun Wanshou and Shao'an were deeply bound in friendship across the years; contemporaries called them Sun and Kong.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the writer Sun Wanshou and Shao'an were deeply bound in friendship across the years; contemporaries called them Sun and Kong.

sentences.zh: 紹安大業末為監察御史。

translations.literal: In the late Daye era Shao'an served as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Daye era Shao'an served as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時高祖為隋討賊於河東，詔紹安監高祖之軍，深見接遇。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozu was suppressing bandits at Hedong for Sui; an edict made Shao'an overseer of Gaozu's army, and he was deeply received and treated.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gaozu was suppressing bandits at Hedong for Sui; an edict made Shao'an overseer of Gaozu's army, and he was deeply received and treated.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，紹安自洛陽間行來奔。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Shao'an came from Luoyang by secret route to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Shao'an came from Luoyang by secret route to join him.

sentences.zh: 高祖見之甚悅，拜內史舍人，賜宅一區、良馬兩匹、錢米絹布等。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased to see him, appointed him Palace Secretary Drafting Clerk, and granted him one residence, two fine horses, and money, rice, silk, and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was greatly pleased to see him, appointed him Palace Secretary Drafting Clerk, and granted him one residence, two fine horses, and money, rice, silk, and cloth.

sentences.zh: 時夏侯端亦嘗為御史，監高祖軍，先紹安歸朝，授秘書監。

translations.literal: At the time Xiahou Duan had also once been a censor overseeing Gaozu's army; before Shao'an he returned to court and was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiahou Duan had also once been a censor overseeing Gaozu's army; before Shao'an he returned to court and was appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 紹安因侍宴，應詔詠《石榴詩》曰：「只為時來晚，開花不及春。」

translations.literal: Shao'an then, while attending a banquet, composed on imperial command the poem On the Pomegranate, saying: "Only because the season came late—its blossoms did not keep pace with spring."
translations.idiomatic: Shao'an then, while attending a banquet, composed on imperial command the poem On the Pomegranate, saying, "Only because the season came late—its blossoms did not keep pace with spring."

sentences.zh: 時人稱之。

translations.literal: Contemporaries praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised it.

sentences.zh: 尋詔撰《梁史》，未成而卒。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered him to compile the History of Liang; he died before completing it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered him to compile the History of Liang; he died before completing it.

sentences.zh: 有文集五卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collected works in five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子 禎

translations.literal: Son Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhen

sentences.zh: 子禎，高宗時為蘇州長史。

translations.literal: Zi Zhen, under Gaozong served as Chief Administrator of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Zhen, under Gaozong served as Chief Administrator of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 曹王明為刺史，不循法度，禎每進諫。

translations.literal: Prince of Cao Li Ming was prefectural governor and did not follow the law; Zhen often remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Cao Li Ming was prefectural governor and did not follow the law; Zhen often remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 明曰：「寡人天子之弟，豈失於為王哉！」

translations.literal: Ming said: "I am the Son of Heaven's younger brother—surely I am not inferior as a prince!"
translations.idiomatic: Ming said, "I am the Son of Heaven's younger brother—surely I am not inferior as a prince!"

sentences.zh: 禎曰：「恩寵不可恃，大王不奉行國命，恐今之榮位，非大王所保，獨不見淮南之事乎？」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Favor and grace cannot be relied upon. If the Great King does not carry out the state's commands, I fear today's honored rank is not what the Great King can keep—have you alone not seen the affair of Huainan?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "Favor and grace cannot be relied upon. If the Great King does not carry out the state's commands, I fear today's honored rank is not what the Great King can keep—have you alone not seen the affair of Huainan?"

sentences.zh: 明不悅。

translations.literal: Ming was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Ming was displeased.

sentences.zh: 明左右有侵暴下人者，禎捕而杖殺之。

translations.literal: Among Ming's attendants were those who tyrannized the people below; Zhen seized and beat them to death.
translations.idiomatic: Among Ming's attendants were those who tyrannized the people below; Zhen seized and beat them to death.

sentences.zh: 明後果坐法，遷於黔中，謂人曰：「吾愧不用孔長史言，以及於此！」

translations.literal: Ming later indeed fell afoul of the law and was moved to Qianzhong; he said to people: "I am ashamed that I did not heed Director Kong's words, and have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Ming later indeed fell afoul of the law and was moved to Qianzhong; he said to people, "I am ashamed that I did not heed Director Kong's words, and have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 禎累遷絳州刺史，封武昌縣子。

translations.literal: Zhen was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of Jiang Prefecture and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of Jiang Prefecture and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚曰溫。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous title was Wen.

sentences.zh: 子 季詡

translations.literal: Son Ji Xu
translations.idiomatic: Son Ji Xu

sentences.zh: 子季詡，早知名，官至左補闕。

translations.literal: Ji Xu was early renowned and reached Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xu was early renowned and reached Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 孫 若思

translations.literal: Grandson Ruosi
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Ruosi

sentences.zh: 紹安孫若思。

translations.literal: Shao'an's grandson Ruosi.
translations.idiomatic: Shao'an's grandson Ruosi.

sentences.zh: 若思孤，母褚氏親自教訓，遂以學行知名。

translations.literal: Ruosi was orphaned; his mother Lady Chu personally taught and instructed him, and he became renowned for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Ruosi was orphaned; his mother Lady Chu personally taught and instructed him, and he became renowned for learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 年少時，有人賫褚遂良書跡數卷以遺若思，唯受其一卷。

translations.literal: In his youth someone brought several scrolls of Chu Suiliang's calligraphy as a gift to Ruosi; he accepted only one scroll.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth someone brought several scrolls of Chu Suiliang's calligraphy as a gift to Ruosi; he accepted only one scroll.

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「此書當今所重，價比黃金，何不總取？」

translations.literal: The man said: "This writing is prized in the present age, its price equal to gold—why not take them all?"
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "This writing is prized in the present age, its price equal to gold—why not take them all?"

sentences.zh: 若思曰：「若價比金寶，此為多矣！」

translations.literal: Ruosi said: "If the price equals gold and treasure, this is already too much!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruosi said, "If the price equals gold and treasure, this is already too much!"

sentences.zh: 更截去半以還之。

translations.literal: He further cut off half and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: He further cut off half and returned it.

sentences.zh: 明經舉，累遷庫部郎中。

translations.literal: Recommended through the Mingjing examination, he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended through the Mingjing examination, he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 若思常謂人曰：「仕至郎中足矣！」

translations.literal: Ruosi often said to people: "To reach Director is enough!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruosi often said to people, "To reach Director is enough!"

sentences.zh: 至是持一石止水，置於座右，以示有止足之意。

translations.literal: At this he placed a stone of still water before his seat to show his intent of knowing when to stop.
translations.idiomatic: At this he placed a stone of still water before his seat to show his intent of knowing when to stop.

sentences.zh: 尋遷給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，敬暉、桓彥範等知國政，以若思多識故事，所有改革大事及疑議，多訪於若思。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and others managed state affairs; because Ruosi knew many precedents, in all major reforms and doubtful matters they often consulted Ruosi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, Jing Hui, Huan Yanfan, and others managed state affairs; because Ruosi knew many precedents, in all major reforms and doubtful matters they often consulted Ruosi.

sentences.zh: 再轉禮部侍郎，出衛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was twice transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and sent out as Prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and sent out as Prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸州別駕，皆以宗室為之，不為刺史致敬，由是多行不法。

translations.literal: Previously, Vice Prefects of the various prefectures were all members of the imperial clan; the prefect did not show them ceremonial respect, and therefore many acted unlawfully.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Vice Prefects of the various prefectures were all members of the imperial clan; the prefect did not show them ceremonial respect, and therefore many acted unlawfully.

sentences.zh: 若思至州，舉奏別駕李道欽犯狀，請加鞫訊。

translations.literal: When Ruosi reached the prefecture, he memorialized and reported Vice Prefect Li Daoqin's offenses and requested intensified interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruosi reached the prefecture, he memorialized and reported Vice Prefect Li Daoqin's offenses and requested intensified interrogation.

sentences.zh: 乃詔別駕於刺史致禮，自若思始也。

translations.literal: An edict then required Vice Prefects to show ceremonial respect to prefects—beginning with Ruosi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required Vice Prefects to show ceremonial respect to prefects—beginning with Ruosi.

sentences.zh: 俄以清白稱，加銀青光祿大夫，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Soon he was famed for integrity and promoted to Grand Master of Silver and Blue Light, and granted one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was famed for integrity and promoted to Grand Master of Silver and Blue Light, and granted one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 歷汝州刺史、太子右諭德，封梁郡公。

translations.literal: He served as Prefect of Ru Prefecture and Right Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Prefect of Ru Prefecture and Right Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 開元十七年卒，謚曰惠。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan he died; his posthumous title was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan he died; his posthumous title was Hui.

sentences.zh: 袁朗

translations.literal: Yuan Lang
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lang

sentences.zh: 袁朗，雍州長安人，陳尚書左僕射樞之子。

translations.literal: Yuan Lang was a man of Chang'an in Yong Prefecture, son of Shu, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lang was a man of Chang'an in Yong Prefecture, son of Shu, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs of Chen.

sentences.zh: 其先自陳郡仕江左，世為冠族，陳亡徙關中。

translations.literal: His ancestors, from Chen commandery, served in the Jiangzuo and for generations were a leading clan; when Chen fell they moved to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors, from Chen commandery, served in the Jiangzuo and for generations were a leading clan; when Chen fell they moved to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 朗勤學，好屬文。

translations.literal: Lang studied diligently and loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Lang studied diligently and loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 在陳，釋褐秘書郎，甚為尚書令江總所重。

translations.literal: In Chen he entered service as Secretary Gentleman and was greatly valued by Department Director Jiang Zong.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen he entered service as Secretary Gentleman and was greatly valued by Department Director Jiang Zong.

sentences.zh: 嘗制千字詩，當時以為盛作。

translations.literal: He once composed a thousand-character poem, which contemporaries regarded as a great work.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed a thousand-character poem, which contemporaries regarded as a great work.

sentences.zh: 陳後主聞而召入禁中，使為《月賦》，朗染翰立成。

translations.literal: Emperor Houzhu of Chen heard of this and summoned him into the inner palace, ordering him to compose a Rhapsody on the Moon; Lang took up the brush and completed it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Houzhu of Chen heard of this and summoned him into the inner palace, ordering him to compose a Rhapsody on the Moon; Lang took up the brush and completed it at once.

sentences.zh: 後主曰：「觀此賦，謝希逸不能獨美於前矣！」

translations.literal: Houzhu said: "Reading this rhapsody, Xie Xiyi cannot alone claim beauty before it!"
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu said, "Reading this rhapsody, Xie Xiyi cannot alone claim beauty before it!"

sentences.zh: 又使為《芝草》、《嘉蓮》二頌，深見優賞。

translations.literal: He further had him compose two eulogies, On the Spirit Grass and On the Fine Lotus, and deeply favored and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He further had him compose two eulogies, On the Spirit Grass and On the Fine Lotus, and deeply favored and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 歷太子洗馬、德教殿學士，遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent, Academic Scholar of the Hall of Virtuous Teaching, and was promoted to Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent, Academic Scholar of the Hall of Virtuous Teaching, and was promoted to Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，仕隋為尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he served Sui as Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he served Sui as Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 武德初，授齊王文學、祠部郎中，封汝南縣男，再轉給事中。

translations.literal: In the early Wude era he was appointed Literary Companion to Prince of Qi, Director in the Ministry of Sacrifices, enfeoffed as Baron of Runan, and twice transferred to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wude era he was appointed Literary Companion to Prince of Qi, Director in the Ministry of Sacrifices, enfeoffed as Baron of Runan, and twice transferred to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初卒官。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan era he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan era he died in office.

sentences.zh: 太宗為之廢朝一日，謂高士廉曰：「袁朗在任雖近，然其性謹厚，特使人傷惜。」

translations.literal: Taizong suspended court for one day on his account and said to Gao Shilian: "Yuan Lang's tenure, though brief, yet his nature was careful and generous—this especially makes one grieve."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong suspended court for one day on his account and said to Gao Shilian, "Yuan Lang's tenure, though brief, yet his nature was careful and generous—this especially makes one grieve."

sentences.zh: 因敕給其喪事，並存問妻子。

translations.literal: He then ordered his funeral provided and sent inquiries to wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his funeral provided and sent inquiries to wife and children.

sentences.zh: 有文集十四卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in fourteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collected works in fourteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 從父弟 承序

translations.literal: Younger paternal cousin Chengxu
translations.idiomatic: Younger paternal cousin Chengxu

sentences.zh: 從父弟承序，陳尚書僕射憲之子。

translations.literal: Younger paternal cousin Chengxu, son of Xian, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Younger paternal cousin Chengxu, son of Xian, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs of Chen.

sentences.zh: 武德中，齊王元吉聞其名，召為學士。

translations.literal: In the Wude era Prince of Qi Li Yuanji heard his name and summoned him as Academic Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era Prince of Qi Li Yuanji heard his name and summoned him as Academic Scholar.

sentences.zh: 府廢，累轉建昌令。

translations.literal: When the princely establishment was abolished, he was repeatedly transferred to Magistrate of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: When the princely establishment was abolished, he was repeatedly transferred to Magistrate of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 在任清靜，士吏懷之。

translations.literal: In office he was quiet and clean; officials and clerks cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was quiet and clean; officials and clerks cherished him.

sentences.zh: 高宗在籓，太宗選學行之士為其僚屬，謂中書侍郎岑文本曰：「梁、陳名臣，有誰可稱？

translations.literal: When Gaozong was still a prince, Taizong selected men of learning and conduct for his staff and said to Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben: "Among the famous ministers of Liang and Chen, who can be praised?
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was still a prince, Taizong selected men of learning and conduct for his staff and said to Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben, "Among the famous ministers of Liang and Chen, who can be praised?

sentences.zh: 復有子弟堪招引否？」

translations.literal: Are there also sons and younger brothers worth recruiting?"
translations.idiomatic: Are there also sons and younger brothers worth recruiting?"

sentences.zh: 文本因言：「隋師入陳，百司奔散，莫有留者，唯袁憲獨在其主之傍。

translations.literal: Wenben then said: "When Sui's army entered Chen, the hundred offices fled and scattered—none remained; only Yuan Xian alone stayed at his lord's side.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben then said, "When Sui's army entered Chen, the hundred offices fled and scattered—none remained; only Yuan Xian alone stayed at his lord's side.

sentences.zh: 王世充將受隋禪，群僚表請勸進，憲子給事中承家托疾，獨不署名。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong was about to accept Sui's abdication, the assembled officials memorialized urging him to advance; Xian's son Supervising Censor Chengjia feigned illness and alone did not sign.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong was about to accept Sui's abdication, the assembled officials memorialized urging him to advance; Xian's son Supervising Censor Chengjia feigned illness and alone did not sign.

sentences.zh: 此父子足稱忠烈。

translations.literal: This father and son are enough to be called loyal and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: This father and son are enough to be called loyal and resolute.

sentences.zh: 承家弟承序，清貞雅操，實繼先風。」

translations.literal: Chengjia's younger brother Chengxu, of pure and upright elegant conduct, truly continued the ways of his forebears."
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia's younger brother Chengxu, of pure and upright elegant conduct, truly continued the ways of his forebears."

sentences.zh: 由是召守晉王友，仍令侍讀，加授弘文館學士。

translations.literal: On this account he was summoned to serve as Friend to the Prince of Jin, and was further ordered to attend and read, with additional appointment as Academic Scholar of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On this account he was summoned to serve as Friend to the Prince of Jin, and was further ordered to attend and read, with additional appointment as Academic Scholar of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟 利貞

translations.literal: Younger paternal cousin of the same grandfather Li Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Younger paternal cousin of the same grandfather Li Zhen

sentences.zh: 朗從祖弟利貞，陳中書令敬之孫也。

translations.literal: Lang's younger paternal cousin of the same grandfather Li Zhen was grandson of Jing, Director of the Secretariat of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's younger paternal cousin of the same grandfather Li Zhen was grandson of Jing, Director of the Secretariat of Chen.

sentences.zh: 高宗時為太常博士、周王侍讀。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong he was Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Attendant Reader to the Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he was Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Attendant Reader to the Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年，王立為皇太子，百官上禮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong the Zhou Prince was established as Heir Apparent; the hundred officials presented ritual observances.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonglong the Zhou Prince was established as Heir Apparent; the hundred officials presented ritual observances.

sentences.zh: 高宗將會百官及命婦於宣政殿，並設九部伎及散樂。

translations.literal: Gaozong was about to assemble the hundred officials and titled ladies at the Hall of Propagating Governance, and also set up the nine sections of music and miscellaneous entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was about to assemble the hundred officials and titled ladies at the Hall of Propagating Governance, and also set up the nine sections of music and miscellaneous entertainments.

sentences.zh: 利貞上疏諫曰：「臣以前殿正寢，非命婦宴會之地；

translations.literal: Li Zhen submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: "Your subject considers that the main hall in the front is not a place for titled ladies' banquets;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying, "Your subject considers that the main hall in the front is not a place for titled ladies' banquets;

sentences.zh: 象闕路門，非倡優進禦之所。

translations.literal: the Elephant Gate and Road Gate are not places where singers and actors should enter to perform for the throne.
translations.idiomatic: the Elephant Gate and Road Gate are not places where singers and actors should enter to perform for the throne.

sentences.zh: 望詔命婦會於別殿，九部伎從東西門入，散樂一色，伏望停省。

translations.literal: I hope an edict may order titled ladies to assemble in a separate hall, the nine sections of music to enter through the east and west gates, and the miscellaneous entertainments to be of one kind—I humbly hope they may be stopped and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: I hope an edict may order titled ladies to assemble in a separate hall, the nine sections of music to enter through the east and west gates, and the miscellaneous entertainments to be of one kind—I humbly hope they may be stopped and reduced.

sentences.zh: 若於三殿別所，自可備極恩私。

translations.literal: If in a separate hall of the three palaces, one may naturally prepare to the utmost private favor.
translations.idiomatic: If in a separate hall of the three palaces, one may naturally prepare to the utmost private favor.

sentences.zh: 微臣庸蔽，不閑典則，忝預禮司，輕陳狂瞽。」

translations.literal: Your humble subject, benighted and obstructed, unversed in canonical norms, presumptuously holding office in the Ministry of Rites, lightly states this rash blindness."
translations.idiomatic: Your humble subject, benighted and obstructed, unversed in canonical norms, presumptuously holding office in the Ministry of Rites, lightly states this rash blindness."

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，即令移於麟德殿。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his words and immediately ordered the assembly moved to Linde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his words and immediately ordered the assembly moved to Linde Hall.

sentences.zh: 至會日，酒酣，帝使中書侍郎薛元超謂利貞曰：「卿門承忠鯁，能抗疏直言，不加厚賜，何以獎勸！」

translations.literal: On the day of the assembly, when wine had gone deep, the Emperor had Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Yuanchao say to Li Zhen: "Your clan has inherited loyal remonstrance; you were able to submit a forthright memorial—if we do not grant rich reward, how shall we encourage such conduct!"
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the assembly, when wine had gone deep, the Emperor had Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Yuanchao say to Li Zhen, "Your clan has inherited loyal remonstrance; you were able to submit a forthright memorial—if we do not grant rich reward, how shall we encourage such conduct!"

sentences.zh: 賜物百段。

translations.literal: He granted one hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He granted one hundred lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 俄遷祠部員外郎，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Sacrifices and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Sacrifices and died.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，以侍讀恩，追贈秘書少監。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, because of his service as Attendant Reader, he was posthumously promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, because of his service as Attendant Reader, he was posthumously promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朗十三代祖漢司徒滂，滂生魏國郎中、御史大夫渙，渙生晉尚書準，準生東晉右將軍、豫章太守沖，沖生司徒從事中郎耽，耽生瑯邪內史質，質生丹陽尹、宋公長史豹，豹生宋吳郡太守洵，累代有高名重位，前史有傳。

translations.literal: Lang's thirteenth-generation ancestor Pang, Minister of Works of Han; Pang begot Huan, Director of the Bureau of Attendants and Censor-in-Chief of Wei; Huan begot Zhun, Director of the Secretariat of Jin; Zhun begot Chong, General of the Right and Prefect of Yuzhang of Eastern Jin; Chong begot Dan, Attendant of the Secretariat of the Ministry of Works; Dan begot Zhi, Interior Minister of Langye; Zhi begot Bao, Chief Administrator and Senior Clerk of Duke of Song; Bao begot Xun, Prefect of Wu of Song—for generations they had high fame and heavy rank, recorded in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's thirteenth-generation ancestor Pang, Minister of Works of Han; Pang begot Huan, Director of the Bureau of Attendants and Censor-in-Chief of Wei; Huan begot Zhun, Director of the Secretariat of Jin; Zhun begot Chong, General of the Right and Prefect of Yuzhang of Eastern Jin; Chong begot Dan, Attendant of the Secretariat of the Ministry of Works; Dan begot Zhi, Interior Minister of Langye; Zhi begot Bao, Chief Administrator and Senior Clerk of Duke of Song; Bao begot Xun, Prefect of Wu of Song—for generations they had high fame and heavy rank, recorded in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 五代叔祖宋太尉淑，高祖父左僕射、雍州刺史顗，高祖司空察，皆死國難。

translations.literal: Shu, fifth-generation granduncle, Grand Commandant Shu of Song; great-grandfather Yan, Left Vice Director and Prefect of Yong of the Yuan clan; great-great-grandfather Cha, Minister of Works—all died for the state's peril.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, fifth-generation granduncle, Grand Commandant Shu of Song; great-grandfather Yan, Left Vice Director and Prefect of Yong of the Yuan clan; great-great-grandfather Cha, Minister of Works—all died for the state's peril.

sentences.zh: 曾祖梁中書監、司空、穆公昂，仕齊為吳興太守，及梁高祖禪齊，久辭朝命。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Ang, Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Works, Duke Mu, served Qi as Prefect of Wuxing; when Liang's Founder abdicated Qi he long refused court appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Ang, Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Works, Duke Mu, served Qi as Prefect of Wuxing; when Liang's Founder abdicated Qi he long refused court appointment.

sentences.zh: 父樞，叔父憲，仕陳，皆為陳僕射。

translations.literal: Father Shu and paternal uncle Xian both served Chen and were both Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Father Shu and paternal uncle Xian both served Chen and were both Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 叔祖敬，中書令。

translations.literal: Granduncle Jing was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Granduncle Jing was Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及陳亡，憲冒難扶護後主。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Xian braved peril to support and protect Houzhu.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Xian braved peril to support and protect Houzhu.

sentences.zh: 朗自以中外人物，為海內冠族，雖瑯邪王氏繼有臺鼎，而歷朝自為佐命，鄙之不以為伍。

translations.literal: Lang, considering himself among eminent figures within and without, the leading clan within the seas, though the Wang clan of Langye for generations had held the highest offices yet in every dynasty served as supporters of the throne—he despised them and would not rank himself with them.
translations.idiomatic: Lang, considering himself among eminent figures within and without, the leading clan within the seas, though the Wang clan of Langye for generations had held the highest offices yet in every dynasty served as supporters of the throne—he despised them and would not rank himself with them.

sentences.zh: 孫 誼

translations.literal: Grandson Yi
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Yi

sentences.zh: 朗孫誼，又虞世南外孫。

translations.literal: Lang's grandson Yi was also maternal grandson of Yu Shinan.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's grandson Yi was also maternal grandson of Yu Shinan.

sentences.zh: 神功中，為蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Shentong era he was Prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shentong era he was Prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗因視事，司馬、清河張沛通謁，沛即侍中文瓘之子。

translations.literal: Once while conducting affairs he received a visit from Assistant Administrator Zhang Pei of Qinghe; Pei was son of Attendant Zhang Wenchan.
translations.idiomatic: Once while conducting affairs he received a visit from Assistant Administrator Zhang Pei of Qinghe; Pei was son of Attendant Zhang Wenchan.

sentences.zh: 誼揖之曰：「司馬何事？」

translations.literal: Yi bowed to him and said: "Assistant Administrator, what is your business?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi bowed to him and said, "Assistant Administrator, what is your business?"

sentences.zh: 沛曰：「此州得一長史，是隴西李亶，天下甲門。」

translations.literal: Pei said: "This prefecture has gained a Chief Administrator—Li Dan of Longxi, the foremost clan under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Pei said, "This prefecture has gained a Chief Administrator—Li Dan of Longxi, the foremost clan under heaven."

sentences.zh: 誼曰：「司馬何言之失！

translations.literal: Yi said: "Assistant Administrator, how your words err!
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Assistant Administrator, how your words err!

sentences.zh: 門戶須歷代人賢，名節風教，為衣冠顧矚，始可稱舉，老夫是也！

translations.literal: A clan must be illustrious through generations of worthy men, name and integrity and moral teaching, looked to by the gentry and officials—only then may it be praised; I am such a one!
translations.idiomatic: A clan must be illustrious through generations of worthy men, name and integrity and moral teaching, looked to by the gentry and officials—only then may it be praised; I am such a one!

sentences.zh: 夫山東人尚於婚媾，求於祿利；

translations.literal: Men of Shandong value marriage alliances and seek salary and profit;
translations.idiomatic: Men of Shandong value marriage alliances and seek salary and profit;

sentences.zh: 作時柱石，見危授命，則曠代無人。

translations.literal: to serve as the age's pillar and, facing peril, give one's life—in generation after generation there is no such man.
translations.idiomatic: to serve as the age's pillar and, facing peril, give one's life—in generation after generation there is no such man.

sentences.zh: 何可說之，以為門戶！」

translations.literal: How can one speak of that and call it a leading clan!"
translations.idiomatic: How can one speak of that and call it a leading clan!"

sentences.zh: 沛懷慚而退。

translations.literal: Pei withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Pei withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 時人以為口實。

translations.literal: Contemporaries took it as a byword.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries took it as a byword.

sentences.zh: 賀德仁

translations.literal: He Deren
translations.idiomatic: He Deren

sentences.zh: 賀德仁，越州山陰人也。

translations.literal: He Deren was a man of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He Deren was a man of Shanyin in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父朗，陳散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Father Lang, Regular Attendant of the Cavalry of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Father Lang, Regular Attendant of the Cavalry of Chen.

sentences.zh: 德仁少與從兄基俱事國子祭酒周弘正，鹹以詞學見稱。

translations.literal: Deren in youth with his elder cousin of the same clan Ji both studied under Guozi Jijiu Zhou Hongzheng, and both were praised for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Deren in youth with his elder cousin of the same clan Ji both studied under Guozi Jijiu Zhou Hongzheng, and both were praised for literary learning.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「學行可師賀德基，文質彬彬賀德仁。」

translations.literal: People of the time said: "In learning and conduct one may take He Deji as teacher; in literary quality balanced and refined, He Deren."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said, "In learning and conduct one may take He Deji as teacher; in literary quality balanced and refined, He Deren."

sentences.zh: 德仁兄弟八人，時人方之荀氏。

translations.literal: Deren had eight brothers; contemporaries compared them to the Xun clan.
translations.idiomatic: Deren had eight brothers; contemporaries compared them to the Xun clan.

sentences.zh: 陳鄱陽王伯山為會稽太守，改其所居甘滂裏為高陽裏。

translations.literal: Prince of Poyang Li Boshan was Prefect of Kuaiji and changed the lane where they lived, Ganpang Lane, to Gaoyang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Poyang Li Boshan was Prefect of Kuaiji and changed the lane where they lived, Ganpang Lane, to Gaoyang Lane.

sentences.zh: 德仁事陳，至吳興王友。

translations.literal: Deren served Chen up to Friend of the Prince of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Deren served Chen up to Friend of the Prince of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 入隋，僕射楊素薦之，授豫章王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: Entering Sui, Vice Director Yang Su recommended him and appointed him Recorder of the Prince of Yuzhang's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Sui, Vice Director Yang Su recommended him and appointed him Recorder of the Prince of Yuzhang's establishment.

sentences.zh: 王以師資禮之，恩遇甚厚。

translations.literal: The prince treated him with the courtesy due a teacher and favored him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The prince treated him with the courtesy due a teacher and favored him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝即位，豫章王改封齊王，又授齊王府屬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, the Prince of Yuzhang was changed to Prince of Qi, and Deren was again appointed to the Qi princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, the Prince of Yuzhang was changed to Prince of Qi, and Deren was again appointed to the Qi princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 及齊王獲譴，府僚皆被誅責，唯德仁以忠謹免罪，出補河東郡司法。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi was punished, the staff were all executed or punished; only Deren was spared for loyalty and prudence and was sent out as Judicial Official of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qi was punished, the staff were all executed or punished; only Deren was spared for loyalty and prudence and was sent out as Judicial Official of Hedong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 素與隱太子善，及高祖平京師，隱太子封隴西公，用德仁為隴西公友。

translations.literal: Su was on good terms with the Hidden Heir; when Gaozu pacified the capital, the Hidden Heir was enfeoffed Duke of Longxi and Deren was made Friend to the Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Su was on good terms with the Hidden Heir; when Gaozu pacified the capital, the Hidden Heir was enfeoffed Duke of Longxi and Deren was made Friend to the Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太子中舍人，以衰老不習吏事，轉太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent; because of age he was unskilled in clerical affairs, he was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent; because of age he was unskilled in clerical affairs, he was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時蕭德言亦為洗馬，陳子良為右衛率府長史，皆為東宮學士。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Deyan was also Attendant of the Heir Apparent, Chen Ziliang was Senior Clerk of the Right Guard Commandant's office—all were Academic Scholars of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiao Deyan was also Attendant of the Heir Apparent, Chen Ziliang was Senior Clerk of the Right Guard Commandant's office—all were Academic Scholars of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，德仁轉趙王友。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan era Deren was transferred to Friend of the Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan era Deren was transferred to Friend of the Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 無幾，卒，年七十余。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, aged over seventy.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 德仁弟子紀、敳，亦以博學知名。

translations.literal: Deren's disciples Ji and Ao were also renowned for broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Deren's disciples Ji and Ao were also renowned for broad learning.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，紀官至太子洗馬，修《五禮》。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong, Ji reached Attendant of the Heir Apparent and compiled the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, Ji reached Attendant of the Heir Apparent and compiled the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 敳至率更令，兼太子侍讀。

translations.literal: Ao reached Director of the Office of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Attendant Reader to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Ao reached Director of the Office of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Attendant Reader to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並為崇賢館學士，學者榮之。

translations.literal: The brothers were both Academic Scholars of the Hall of Honoring the Worthy; scholars counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were both Academic Scholars of the Hall of Honoring the Worthy; scholars counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 庾抱

translations.literal: Yu Bao
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bao

sentences.zh: 庾抱，潤州江寧人也，其先自潁川徙家焉。

translations.literal: Yu Bao was a man of Jiangning in Run Prefecture; his ancestors moved their household there from Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bao was a man of Jiangning in Run Prefecture; his ancestors moved their household there from Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 祖眾，陳御史中丞。

translations.literal: Grandfather Zhong, Vice Censor-in-Chief of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Zhong, Vice Censor-in-Chief of Chen.

sentences.zh: 父超，南平王記室。

translations.literal: Father Chao, Recorder of the Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Father Chao, Recorder of the Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 抱開皇中為延州參軍事。

translations.literal: Bao in the Kaihuang era was Military Adjutant of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bao in the Kaihuang era was Military Adjutant of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後累歲，調吏部。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尚書牛弘知其有學術，給筆劄令自序。

translations.literal: Director Niu Hong knew he had scholarship and gave him brush and paper ordering him to compose his own autobiography.
translations.idiomatic: Director Niu Hong knew he had scholarship and gave him brush and paper ordering him to compose his own autobiography.

sentences.zh: 援翰便就，弘甚奇之。

translations.literal: He took up the brush and finished at once; Hong marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: He took up the brush and finished at once; Hong marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 後補元德太子學士，禮賜甚優。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Academic Scholar to the Heir Apparent Yuande and was generously rewarded by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Academic Scholar to the Heir Apparent Yuande and was generously rewarded by ritual.

sentences.zh: 會皇孫載誕，太子宴賓客，抱於坐中獻《嫡皇孫頌》，深被嗟賞。

translations.literal: When the imperial grandson was born, the Heir Apparent feasted guests; Bao at the seat presented the Eulogy on the Heir Apparent's Grandson and was deeply praised.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial grandson was born, the Heir Apparent feasted guests; Bao at the seat presented the Eulogy on the Heir Apparent's Grandson and was deeply praised.

sentences.zh: 後為越巂主簿，稱病不行。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief Clerk of Yuexi and claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Chief Clerk of Yuexi and claimed illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 義寧中，隱太子弘引為隴西公府記室。

translations.literal: In the Yining era the Hidden Heir Hong summoned him as Recorder of the Duke of Longxi's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yining era the Hidden Heir Hong summoned him as Recorder of the Duke of Longxi's establishment.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多務，公府文檄皆出於抱。

translations.literal: At the time military and state affairs were many; all the establishment's documents and proclamations came from Bao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time military and state affairs were many; all the establishment's documents and proclamations came from Bao.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太子舍人，未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent; before long he died.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collection in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 蔡允恭

translations.literal: Cai Yungong
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yungong

sentences.zh: 蔡允恭，荊州江陵人也。

translations.literal: Cai Yungong was a man of Jiangling in Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yungong was a man of Jiangling in Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖點，梁尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: Grandfather Dian, Director in the Ministry of Rites of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Dian, Director in the Ministry of Rites of Liang.

sentences.zh: 父大業，後梁左民尚書。

translations.literal: Father Daye, Left Minister of the People of Later Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Father Daye, Left Minister of the People of Later Liang.

sentences.zh: 允恭有風彩，善綴文。

translations.literal: Yungong had elegant bearing and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong had elegant bearing and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 仕隋歷著作佐郎、起居舍人。

translations.literal: Serving Sui he held the posts of Assistant Director of the Palace Library and Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Sui he held the posts of Assistant Director of the Palace Library and Diarist.

sentences.zh: 雅善吟詠。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at chanting poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at chanting poetry.

sentences.zh: 煬帝屬詞賦，多令諷誦之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang composed lyric rhapsodies he often had Yungong recite them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang composed lyric rhapsodies he often had Yungong recite them.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣教宮女，允恭深以為恥，因稱氣疾，不時應召。

translations.literal: Once he was ordered to teach palace women; Yungong was deeply shamed by this and claimed a breathing disorder, not answering summons in season.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was ordered to teach palace women; Yungong was deeply shamed by this and claimed a breathing disorder, not answering summons in season.

sentences.zh: 煬帝又許授以內史舍人，更令入內教宮人，允恭固辭不就，以是稍被疏絕。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang also promised to appoint him Palace Secretary Drafting Clerk, then again ordered him to enter the inner palace to teach palace women; Yungong firmly declined and would not accept, and on this account was gradually estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang also promised to appoint him Palace Secretary Drafting Clerk, then again ordered him to enter the inner palace to teach palace women; Yungong firmly declined and would not accept, and on this account was gradually estranged.

sentences.zh: 江都之難，允恭從宇文化及西上，沒於竇建德。

translations.literal: In the disaster at Jiangdu, Yungong followed Yuwen Huaji westward and was lost to Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: In the disaster at Jiangdu, Yungong followed Yuwen Huaji westward and was lost to Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 及平東夏，太宗引為秦府參軍，兼文學館學士。

translations.literal: When the eastern Xia was pacified, Taizong summoned him as Staff Member of the Prince of Qin's establishment and concurrently Academic Scholar of the Hall of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern Xia was pacified, Taizong summoned him as Staff Member of the Prince of Qin's establishment and concurrently Academic Scholar of the Hall of Literature.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，除太子洗馬。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan era he was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan era he was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋致仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon he retired and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷，又撰《後梁春秋》十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection in ten scrolls, and also compiled the Spring and Autumn of Later Liang in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collection in ten scrolls, and also compiled the Spring and Autumn of Later Liang in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 鄭世翼

translations.literal: Zheng Shiyi
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shiyi

sentences.zh: 鄭世翼，鄭州滎陽人也，世為著姓。

translations.literal: Zheng Shiyi was a man of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture; for generations his clan was a distinguished surname.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shiyi was a man of Xingyang in Zheng Prefecture; for generations his clan was a distinguished surname.

sentences.zh: 祖敬德，周儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Grandfather Jingde, Regiment Commander of the Same Rank of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Jingde, Regiment Commander of the Same Rank of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父機，司武中士。

translations.literal: Father Ji, Central Warrior Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Father Ji, Central Warrior Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 世翼弱冠有盛名。

translations.literal: Shiyi at twenty sui already had great fame.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi at twenty sui already had great fame.

sentences.zh: 武德中，歷萬年丞、揚州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In the Wude era he served successively as Assistant Magistrate of Wannian and Recording Officer of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era he served successively as Assistant Magistrate of Wannian and Recording Officer of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 數以言辭忤物，稱為輕薄。

translations.literal: Several times with words he offended others and was called frivolous.
translations.idiomatic: Several times with words he offended others and was called frivolous.

sentences.zh: 時崔信明自謂文章獨步，多所淩轢；

translations.literal: At the time Cui Xinming considered his own writing without peer and often looked down on others;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cui Xinming considered his own writing without peer and often looked down on others;

sentences.zh: 世翼遇諸江中，謂之曰：「嘗聞『楓落吳江冷。』」

translations.literal: Shiyi met him on the river and said to him: "I once heard 'Maples fall on the cold Wu River.'"
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi met him on the river and said to him, "I once heard 'Maples fall on the cold Wu River.'"

sentences.zh: 信明欣然示百余篇。

translations.literal: Xinming gladly showed him more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Xinming gladly showed him more than a hundred pieces.

sentences.zh: 世翼覽之未終，曰：「所見不如所聞。」

translations.literal: Shiyi had not finished reading them when he said: "What one sees is not as good as what one hears."
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi had not finished reading them when he said, "What one sees is not as good as what one hears."

sentences.zh: 投之於江，信明不能對，擁楫而去。

translations.literal: He threw them into the river; Xinming could not reply and rowed away holding the oars.
translations.idiomatic: He threw them into the river; Xinming could not reply and rowed away holding the oars.

sentences.zh: 世翼貞觀中坐怨謗，配流巂州，卒。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era Shiyi was punished for slander and exiled to Zui Prefecture, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era Shiyi was punished for slander and exiled to Zui Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 文集多遺失，撰《交遊傳》，頗行於時。

translations.literal: Much of his collected works was lost; he compiled Records of Friendships, which circulated widely in its time.
translations.idiomatic: Much of his collected works was lost; he compiled Records of Friendships, which circulated widely in its time.

sentences.zh: 謝偃

translations.literal: Xie Yan
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan

sentences.zh: 謝偃，衛縣人也，本姓直勒氏。

translations.literal: Xie Yan was a man of Wei County; his original surname was Zhile.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan was a man of Wei County; his original surname was Zhile.

sentences.zh: 祖孝政，北齊散騎常侍，改姓謝氏。

translations.literal: Grandfather Xiaozheng, Regular Attendant of the Cavalry of Northern Qi, changed the surname to Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Xiaozheng, Regular Attendant of the Cavalry of Northern Qi, changed the surname to Xie.

sentences.zh: 偃仕隋為散從正員郎。

translations.literal: Yan served Sui as Regular Gentleman of the Cavalry Retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Yan served Sui as Regular Gentleman of the Cavalry Retinue.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，應詔對策及第，歷高陵主簿。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan era he passed the imperial policy examination and served successively as Chief Clerk of Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenguan era he passed the imperial policy examination and served successively as Chief Clerk of Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 十一年，駕幸東都，谷、洛泛溢洛陽宮，詔求直諫之士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Emperor's carriage visited the Eastern Capital; the Gu and Luo rivers overflowed into Luoyang Palace; an edict sought men of straight remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Emperor's carriage visited the Eastern Capital; the Gu and Luo rivers overflowed into Luoyang Palace; an edict sought men of straight remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 偃上封事，極言得失。

translations.literal: Yan submitted a sealed memorial, speaking exhaustively of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Yan submitted a sealed memorial, speaking exhaustively of gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 太宗稱善，引為弘文館直學士，拜魏王府功曹。

translations.literal: Taizong praised it and summoned him as Direct Academic Scholar of the Hongwen Hall and appointed him Merit Officer of the Prince of Wei's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised it and summoned him as Direct Academic Scholar of the Hongwen Hall and appointed him Merit Officer of the Prince of Wei's establishment.

sentences.zh: 偃嘗為《塵》、《影》二賦，甚工。

translations.literal: Yan once composed the two rhapsodies Dust and Shadow, very skillfully done.
translations.idiomatic: Yan once composed the two rhapsodies Dust and Shadow, very skillfully done.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而詔見，自制賦序，言「區宇乂安，功德茂盛」。

translations.literal: Taizong heard of this and summoned him by edict, himself composing a preface to the rhapsody saying "the realm is at peace and merit abundant."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong heard of this and summoned him by edict, himself composing a preface to the rhapsody saying "the realm is at peace and merit abundant."

sentences.zh: 令其為賦，偃奉詔撰成，名曰《述聖賦》，賜采數十匹。

translations.literal: He ordered Yan to compose the rhapsody; Yan received the edict and completed it, titled Rhapsody Recounting Sagely Virtue, and was granted several dozen bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yan to compose the rhapsody; Yan received the edict and completed it, titled Rhapsody Recounting Sagely Virtue, and was granted several dozen bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 偃又獻《惟皇誡德賦》以申諷，曰：

translations.literal: Yan also presented the Rhapsody Admonishing Sagely Virtue to offer indirect remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yan also presented the Rhapsody Admonishing Sagely Virtue to offer indirect remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞理忘亂，安忘危，逸忘勞，得忘失。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that in order one forgets disorder, in peace one forgets peril, in ease one forgets toil, in gain one forgets loss.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that in order one forgets disorder, in peace one forgets peril, in ease one forgets toil, in gain one forgets loss.

sentences.zh: 此四者，人君莫不皆然。

translations.literal: These four—no ruler fails to be so.
translations.idiomatic: These four—no ruler fails to be so.

sentences.zh: 是以夏桀以瑤臺璇室為麗，而不悟鳴條南巢之禍；

translations.literal: Therefore Jie of Xia took the jade tower and chamber of luster as splendor yet did not perceive the disaster of Mingtiao and southern nest;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Jie of Xia took the jade tower and chamber of luster as splendor yet did not perceive the disaster of Mingtiao and southern nest;

sentences.zh: 殷辛以象箸玉杯為華，而不知牧野白旗之敗。

translations.literal: Xin of Yin took ivory chopsticks and jade cups as glory yet did not know the defeat of the white banners at Muye.
translations.idiomatic: Xin of Yin took ivory chopsticks and jade cups as glory yet did not know the defeat of the white banners at Muye.

sentences.zh: 故當其盛也，謂四海為己力；

translations.literal: When they were flourishing they considered the four seas their own strength;
translations.idiomatic: When they were flourishing they considered the four seas their own strength;

sentences.zh: 及其衰焉，乃匹夫之不制。

translations.literal: when they declined, not even a common man could control them.
translations.idiomatic: when they declined, not even a common man could control them.

sentences.zh: 當其信也，謂天下為無危；

translations.literal: When they trusted, they considered the realm without peril;
translations.idiomatic: When they trusted, they considered the realm without peril;

sentences.zh: 及其疑也，則顧盼皆仇敵。

translations.literal: when they grew suspicious, every glance became an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: when they grew suspicious, every glance became an enemy.

sentences.zh: 是知必有其德，則誠結戎夷，化行荒裔。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that if there is virtue, sincerity binds the Rong and Yi and teaching spreads to remote regions.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows that if there is virtue, sincerity binds the Rong and Yi and teaching spreads to remote regions.

sentences.zh: 茍失其度，則變生骨肉，釁起腹心矣！

translations.literal: If one loses measure, change arises among flesh and blood and strife begins in the heart!
translations.idiomatic: If one loses measure, change arises among flesh and blood and strife begins in the heart!

sentences.zh: 是以為人主者，不可忘初。

translations.literal: Therefore one who is lord of men must not forget the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one who is lord of men must not forget the beginning.

sentences.zh: 處殿堂，則思前主之所以亡；

translations.literal: Dwelling in halls and chambers, then think how former lords came to perish;
translations.idiomatic: Dwelling in halls and chambers, then think how former lords came to perish;

sentences.zh: 朝萬國，則思今己之所以貴；

translations.literal: holding court for the myriad states, then think how you yourself came to honor today;
translations.idiomatic: holding court for the myriad states, then think how you yourself came to honor today;

sentences.zh: 巡府庫，則思今己之所以得；

translations.literal: touring the storehouses, then think how you yourself came to obtain them today;
translations.idiomatic: touring the storehouses, then think how you yourself came to obtain them today;

sentences.zh: 視功臣，則思其為己之始；

translations.literal: viewing meritorious ministers, then think how they began for you;
translations.idiomatic: viewing meritorious ministers, then think how they began for you;

sentences.zh: 見名將，則思其用力之初。

translations.literal: seeing famous generals, then think how they exerted strength at the start.
translations.idiomatic: seeing famous generals, then think how they exerted strength at the start.

sentences.zh: 茍弗忘舊，則人無易心，何患乎天下之不化！

translations.literal: If one does not forget the old, then people will not change heart—what worry that the realm will not be transformed!
translations.idiomatic: If one does not forget the old, then people will not change heart—what worry that the realm will not be transformed!

sentences.zh: 故旦行之則為堯、舜，暮失之則為桀、紂，豈異人哉！

translations.literal: Morning practice makes Yao and Shun; evening loss makes Jie and Zhou—is the man different!
translations.idiomatic: Morning practice makes Yao and Shun; evening loss makes Jie and Zhou—is the man different!

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: The words say:
translations.idiomatic: The words say:

sentences.zh: 周墳籍以遷觀，總宇宙而一窺；

translations.literal: Through Zhou's written records I look down and up, surveying the cosmos at a glance;
translations.idiomatic: Through Zhou's written records I look down and up, surveying the cosmos at a glance;

sentences.zh: 結繩往而莫紀，書契崇而可知。

translations.literal: the age of knotted cords passed unrecorded; when script was honored it could be known.
translations.idiomatic: the age of knotted cords passed unrecorded; when script was honored it could be known.

sentences.zh: 惟皇王之叠代，信步驟之恆規，莫不慮失者常得，懷安者必危。

translations.literal: Through generations of emperors and kings, truly the constant rule of step and pace—none failed to consider that the one who loses always gains, the one who rests in peace always faces peril.
translations.idiomatic: Through generations of emperors and kings, truly the constant rule of step and pace—none failed to consider that the one who loses always gains, the one who rests in peace always faces peril.

sentences.zh: 是以戰戰怵怵，日慎一日，守約守儉，去奢去逸。

translations.literal: Therefore trembling and fearful, daily cautious day by day, keeping covenant and thrift, casting off extravagance and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore trembling and fearful, daily cautious day by day, keeping covenant and thrift, casting off extravagance and ease.

sentences.zh: 外無荒禽，內無荒色，唯賢是授，唯人斯恤。

translations.literal: Without wild birds without, without wild colors within; only the worthy are appointed, only people are cherished.
translations.idiomatic: Without wild birds without, without wild colors within; only the worthy are appointed, only people are cherished.

sentences.zh: 則三皇不足六，五帝不足十。

translations.literal: Then the Three Sovereigns are not enough for six, the Five Emperors not enough for ten.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Three Sovereigns are not enough for six, the Five Emperors not enough for ten.

sentences.zh: 若夫恃聖驕力，狠戾倔強，忠良是棄，諂佞斯獎。

translations.literal: If one relies on sagely power and is arrogant, cruel and obstinate, abandoning the loyal and good and rewarding flattery and sycophancy.
translations.idiomatic: If one relies on sagely power and is arrogant, cruel and obstinate, abandoning the loyal and good and rewarding flattery and sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 構崇臺以造天，穿深池以絕壤。

translations.literal: Building lofty towers to reach heaven, digging deep pools to cut through earth.
translations.idiomatic: Building lofty towers to reach heaven, digging deep pools to cut through earth.

sentences.zh: 厚賦重斂，積寶藏鏹；

translations.literal: Heavy taxes and repeated levies, amassing treasure and hoarding coin;
translations.idiomatic: Heavy taxes and repeated levies, amassing treasure and hoarding coin;

sentences.zh: 無罪加刑，有功不賞。

translations.literal: punishing the guiltless, not rewarding the meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: punishing the guiltless, not rewarding the meritorious.

sentences.zh: 則夏桀可二，殷辛易兩。

translations.literal: Then Jie of Xia could be doubled, and Xin of Yin easily paired.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jie of Xia could be doubled, and Xin of Yin easily paired.

sentences.zh: 在危所恃，居安勿忘。

translations.literal: In peril rely on what you rely on; in peace do not forget.
translations.idiomatic: In peril rely on what you rely on; in peace do not forget.

sentences.zh: 功臣無逐，故人無放。

translations.literal: Do not drive away meritorious ministers; do not banish old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Do not drive away meritorious ministers; do not banish old friends.

sentences.zh: 放故者亡，逐功者喪。

translations.literal: Banish old friends and perish; drive away the meritorious and lose.
translations.idiomatic: Banish old friends and perish; drive away the meritorious and lose.

sentences.zh: 四海岌岌，九土漫漫，覆之甚易，存之實難。

translations.literal: The four seas precarious, the nine regions vast—overturning is very easy, preserving is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: The four seas precarious, the nine regions vast—overturning is very easy, preserving is truly hard.

sentences.zh: 是以一人有悅，萬國同歡；

translations.literal: Therefore when one man has joy, the myriad states share gladness;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when one man has joy, the myriad states share gladness;

sentences.zh: 一人失所，兆庶俱殘。

translations.literal: when one man loses his place, the multitude all suffer.
translations.idiomatic: when one man loses his place, the multitude all suffer.

sentences.zh: 喜則隆冬可熱，怒則盛夏成寒；

translations.literal: Joy can warm deep winter; anger can freeze midsummer;
translations.idiomatic: Joy can warm deep winter; anger can freeze midsummer;

sentences.zh: 一動而八表亂，一言而天下安。

translations.literal: one movement and the eight directions are disturbed, one word and the realm is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: one movement and the eight directions are disturbed, one word and the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 舉君過者曰忠，述主美者為佞，茍承顏以順旨，必蔽視而稱聖。

translations.literal: One who cites the ruler's faults is called loyal; one who recounts the lord's beauties is called sycophantic—if one merely accepts countenance and follows intent, one must blind the eyes and call him sage.
translations.idiomatic: One who cites the ruler's faults is called loyal; one who recounts the lord's beauties is called sycophantic—if one merely accepts countenance and follows intent, one must blind the eyes and call him sage.

sentences.zh: 故使曲者亂直，邪者疑正；

translations.literal: Thus the crooked confound the straight, the perverse make the upright doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the crooked confound the straight, the perverse make the upright doubt;

sentences.zh: 改華服以就胡，變雅音而入鄭；

translations.literal: changing elegant dress to follow the Hu, changing refined tones to enter the Zheng;
translations.idiomatic: changing elegant dress to follow the Hu, changing refined tones to enter the Zheng;

sentences.zh: 雖往古之軌躅，亦當今之龜鏡。

translations.literal: though the tracks of antiquity, they are also mirrors for the present age.
translations.idiomatic: though the tracks of antiquity, they are also mirrors for the present age.

sentences.zh: 崔嵬龍殿，赫奕鳳門，苞四海以稱主，冠天下而獨尊。

translations.literal: Towering dragon halls, blazing phoenix gates—embracing the four seas to call oneself lord, topping the realm to stand alone in honor.
translations.idiomatic: Towering dragon halls, blazing phoenix gates—embracing the four seas to call oneself lord, topping the realm to stand alone in honor.

sentences.zh: 既兄日而姊月，亦父乾而母坤。

translations.literal: Already elder brother to sun and elder sister to moon, also father to Qian and mother to Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Already elder brother to sun and elder sister to moon, also father to Qian and mother to Kun.

sentences.zh: 視則金翠溢目，聽則絲竹盈耳。

translations.literal: Looking, gold and kingfisher fill the eyes; listening, silk and bamboo fill the ears.
translations.idiomatic: Looking, gold and kingfisher fill the eyes; listening, silk and bamboo fill the ears.

sentences.zh: 信賞罰之在躬，實榮辱之由己；

translations.literal: Truly reward and punishment rest on the person, truly glory and shame come from oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Truly reward and punishment rest on the person, truly glory and shame come from oneself;

sentences.zh: 語義皇而易匹，言堯、舜之可擬。

translations.literal: speaking of the sage-emperors and easily matching them, saying Yao and Shun can be compared.
translations.idiomatic: speaking of the sage-emperors and easily matching them, saying Yao and Shun can be compared.

sentences.zh: 驕誌自此而生，侈心因茲而起。

translations.literal: Arrogance and ambition arise from this; extravagant heart springs from here.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogance and ambition arise from this; extravagant heart springs from here.

sentences.zh: 常懼覆而懼亡，必思足而思止；

translations.literal: Constantly fearing overturn and fearing loss, one must think sufficiency and think stopping;
translations.idiomatic: Constantly fearing overturn and fearing loss, one must think sufficiency and think stopping;

sentences.zh: 勿忘潛龍之初，當懷布衣之始。

translations.literal: Do not forget the beginning when the hidden dragon rose; always cherish the beginning in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Do not forget the beginning when the hidden dragon rose; always cherish the beginning in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 在位稱寶，居器曰神，鐘鼓庭設，玉帛階陳。

translations.literal: In office called treasure, in vessel called spirit; bells and drums set in the court, jade and silk arrayed on the steps.
translations.idiomatic: In office called treasure, in vessel called spirit; bells and drums set in the court, jade and silk arrayed on the steps.

sentences.zh: 得必有兆，失必有因；

translations.literal: Gain always has omens, loss always has cause;
translations.idiomatic: Gain always has omens, loss always has cause;

sentences.zh: 一替一立，或周或秦。

translations.literal: one falls one rises, now Zhou now Qin.
translations.idiomatic: one falls one rises, now Zhou now Qin.

sentences.zh: 既承前代，當思後人。

translations.literal: Having succeeded the former age, one must think of later men.
translations.idiomatic: Having succeeded the former age, one must think of later men.

sentences.zh: 唯德可以久，天道無常親。

translations.literal: Only virtue can long endure; the Way of Heaven has no constant favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Only virtue can long endure; the Way of Heaven has no constant favorites.

sentences.zh: 時李百藥工為五言詩，而偃善作賦，時人稱為李詩謝賦焉。

translations.literal: At the time Li Baiyao was skilled at five-character poetry while Yan was skilled at composing rhapsodies; contemporaries called them Li's poems and Xie's rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Baiyao was skilled at five-character poetry while Yan was skilled at composing rhapsodies; contemporaries called them Li's poems and Xie's rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 十七年，府廢，出為湘潭令，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the establishment was abolished and he was sent out as Magistrate of Xiangtan, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the establishment was abolished and he was sent out as Magistrate of Xiangtan, where he died.

sentences.zh: 文集十卷。

translations.literal: Collected works in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Collected works in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 崔信明

translations.literal: Cui Xinming
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xinming

sentences.zh: 崔信明，青州益都人也，後魏七兵尚書光伯曾孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Xinming was a man of Yidu in Qing Prefecture, great-grandson of Guangbo, Director of the Seven Armies of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xinming was a man of Yidu in Qing Prefecture, great-grandson of Guangbo, Director of the Seven Armies of Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖縚，北海郡守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Shao, Prefect of Beihai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Shao, Prefect of Beihai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 信明以五月五日日正中時生，有異雀數頭，身形甚小，五色畢備，集於庭樹；

translations.literal: Xinming was born at the exact noon of the fifth day of the fifth month; several strange birds, very small in body, complete in five colors, gathered on the courtyard tree;
translations.idiomatic: Xinming was born at the exact noon of the fifth day of the fifth month; several strange birds, very small in body, complete in five colors, gathered on the courtyard tree;

sentences.zh: 鼓翼齊鳴，聲清宛亮。

translations.literal: beating wings they sang together, the sound clear, mellow, and bright.
translations.idiomatic: beating wings they sang together, the sound clear, mellow, and bright.

sentences.zh: 隋太史令史良使至青州，遇而占之曰：「五月為火，火為《離》，《離》為文彩。

translations.literal: Sui Grand Astrologer Ling Shi Liang sent an envoy to Qing Prefecture; encountering him he divined and said: "The fifth month is fire; fire is Li; Li is literary splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Grand Astrologer Ling Shi Liang sent an envoy to Qing Prefecture; encountering him he divined and said, "The fifth month is fire; fire is Li; Li is literary splendor.
