sentences.zh: 日正中，文之盛也。

translations.literal: Noon is the fullness of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Noon is the fullness of writing.

sentences.zh: 又有雀五色，奮翼而鳴。

translations.literal: Also there are birds of five colors, beating wings and singing.
translations.idiomatic: Also there are birds of five colors, beating wings and singing.

sentences.zh: 此兒必文藻煥爛，聲名播於天下。

translations.literal: This child will surely have brilliant literary ornament; fame will spread through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: This child will surely have brilliant literary ornament; fame will spread through the realm.

sentences.zh: 雀形既小，祿位殆不高。」

translations.literal: The birds' forms being small, rank and salary will probably not be high."
translations.idiomatic: The birds' forms being small, rank and salary will probably not be high."

sentences.zh: 及長，博聞強記，下筆成章。

translations.literal: When grown he was broadly learned with strong memory; taking up the brush he completed compositions.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was broadly learned with strong memory; taking up the brush he completed compositions.

sentences.zh: 鄉人高孝基有知人之鑒，每謂人曰：「崔信明才學富贍，雖名冠一時，但恨其位不達耳！」

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Gao Xiaoji had the discernment to know men and often said to people: "Cui Xinming's talent and learning are rich and ample; though his name tops the age, one regrets only that his rank did not reach high!"
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Gao Xiaoji had the discernment to know men and often said to people, "Cui Xinming's talent and learning are rich and ample; though his name tops the age, one regrets only that his rank did not reach high!"

sentences.zh: 大業中，為堯城令。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was Magistrate of Yaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he was Magistrate of Yaocheng.

sentences.zh: 竇建德僭號，欲引用之。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande usurped title and wished to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande usurped title and wished to employ him.

sentences.zh: 信明族弟敬素為建德鴻臚卿，說信明曰：「隋主無道，天下鼎沸，衣冠禮樂，掃地無余。

translations.literal: Xinming's clansman younger brother Jingsu was Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments of Jiande and said to Xinming: "The Sui ruler was without the Way; the realm boils over; ritual, music, robes, and caps are swept away without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Xinming's clansman younger brother Jingsu was Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments of Jiande and said to Xinming, "The Sui ruler was without the Way; the realm boils over; ritual, music, robes, and caps are swept away without remainder.

sentences.zh: 兄遁跡下僚，不被收用，豫讓所以不報範中行，只以眾人遇我者也。

translations.literal: Elder brother, hiding in low office, not being employed—this is why Yu Rang did not repay Fan Zhonghang: he was merely treated as one of the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother, hiding in low office, not being employed—this is why Yu Rang did not repay Fan Zhonghang: he was merely treated as one of the crowd.

sentences.zh: 夏王英武，有並吞天下之心，士女繈負而至者，不可稱數。

translations.literal: King Xia is heroic and martial, with the mind to swallow the realm; men and women come carrying infants on their backs beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: King Xia is heroic and martial, with the mind to swallow the realm; men and women come carrying infants on their backs beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 此時不立功立事，豈是見幾而作者乎？」

translations.literal: At this time not to establish merit and affairs—can this be one who sees the moment and acts?"
translations.idiomatic: At this time not to establish merit and affairs—can this be one who sees the moment and acts?"

sentences.zh: 信明曰：「昔申胥海畔漁者，尚能固其節；

translations.literal: Xinming said: "Formerly Shen Xu at the seashore was a fisherman yet could hold fast to his integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Xinming said, "Formerly Shen Xu at the seashore was a fisherman yet could hold fast to his integrity;

sentences.zh: 吾終不能屈身偽主，求斗筲之職。」

translations.literal: I ultimately cannot bow to a false lord to seek an office of a peck and dipper."
translations.idiomatic: I ultimately cannot bow to a false lord to seek an office of a peck and dipper."

sentences.zh: 遂逾城而遁，隱於太行山。

translations.literal: He then crossed the wall and fled, hiding on Mount Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the wall and fled, hiding on Mount Taihang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，應詔舉，授興世丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan he was recommended by imperial edict and appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan he was recommended by imperial edict and appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 遷秦川令，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Magistrate of Qinchuan and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Magistrate of Qinchuan and died.

sentences.zh: 信明頗蹇傲自伐，常賦詩吟嘯，自謂過於李百藥，時人多不許之。

translations.literal: Xinming was quite proud and self-congratulatory, often composing poetry and chanting, considering himself superior to Li Baiyao; many contemporaries did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xinming was quite proud and self-congratulatory, often composing poetry and chanting, considering himself superior to Li Baiyao; many contemporaries did not agree.

sentences.zh: 又矜其門族，輕侮四海士望，由是為世所譏。

translations.literal: He also prided himself on his clan and lightly insulted eminent scholars throughout the realm; on this account he was mocked by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He also prided himself on his clan and lightly insulted eminent scholars throughout the realm; on this account he was mocked by the age.

sentences.zh: 子 冬日

translations.literal: Son Dongri
translations.idiomatic: Son Dongri

sentences.zh: 子冬日，則天時為黃門侍郎，被酷吏所殺。

translations.literal: Son Dongri, under Zetian was Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and was killed by cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: Son Dongri, under Zetian was Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and was killed by cruel officials.

sentences.zh: 張蘊古

translations.literal: Zhang Yungu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yungu

sentences.zh: 張蘊古，相州洹水人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yungu was a man of Huanshui in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yungu was a man of Huanshui in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，博涉書傳，善綴文，能背碑覆局。

translations.literal: By nature intelligent and keen, he broadly studied written records, was skilled at literary composition, and could recite stele texts from memory and replay chess positions from memory.
translations.idiomatic: By nature intelligent and keen, he broadly studied written records, was skilled at literary composition, and could recite stele texts from memory and replay chess positions from memory.

sentences.zh: 尤曉時務，為州閭所稱。

translations.literal: He was especially versed in current affairs and was praised by his district.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially versed in current affairs and was praised by his district.

sentences.zh: 自幽州總管府記室直中書省。

translations.literal: From Recorder of the Youzhou General Headquarters he went directly to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From Recorder of the Youzhou General Headquarters he went directly to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太宗初即位，上《大寶箴》以諷，其詞曰：

translations.literal: When Taizong first took the throne, he submitted the Great Treasure Admonition to offer indirect remonstrance; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong first took the throne, he submitted the Great Treasure Admonition to offer indirect remonstrance; its words say:

sentences.zh: 今來古往，俯察仰觀，惟辟作福，為君實難。

translations.literal: Now past and present, looking down and looking up—only the lord makes blessing; to be lord is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: Now past and present, looking down and looking up—only the lord makes blessing; to be lord is truly hard.

sentences.zh: 主普天之下，處王公之上；

translations.literal: Presiding over all under heaven, dwelling above kings and dukes;
translations.idiomatic: Presiding over all under heaven, dwelling above kings and dukes;

sentences.zh: 任土貢其所求，具僚和其所唱。

translations.literal: each region submits what it seeks, all officials harmonize what they sing.
translations.idiomatic: each region submits what it seeks, all officials harmonize what they sing.

sentences.zh: 是故競懼之心日弛，邪僻之情轉放，豈知事起乎所忽，禍生乎無妄。

translations.literal: Therefore the mind of competing fear daily slackens, feelings of perversity daily expand—who knows trouble rises from what is neglected, disaster born from the unlooked-for.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the mind of competing fear daily slackens, feelings of perversity daily expand—who knows trouble rises from what is neglected, disaster born from the unlooked-for.

sentences.zh: 固以聖人受命，拯溺亨屯，歸過於己，推恩於民。

translations.literal: Truly the sage receives mandate, rescues the drowning and prospers the stranded, attributing fault to himself and extending grace to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Truly the sage receives mandate, rescues the drowning and prospers the stranded, attributing fault to himself and extending grace to the people.

sentences.zh: 大明無偏照，至公無私親。

translations.literal: Great brightness has no partial shining; supreme fairness has no private kin.
translations.idiomatic: Great brightness has no partial shining; supreme fairness has no private kin.

sentences.zh: 故以一人治天下，不以天下奉一人。

translations.literal: Therefore one man governs the realm; the realm does not serve one man.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one man governs the realm; the realm does not serve one man.

sentences.zh: 禮以禁其奢，樂以防其佚。

translations.literal: Rites forbid extravagance; music guards against dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: Rites forbid extravagance; music guards against dissipation.

sentences.zh: 左言而右事，出警而入蹕。

translations.literal: Words left, affairs right; going out with guard, entering with imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: Words left, affairs right; going out with guard, entering with imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 四時同其慘舒，三光同其得失。

translations.literal: The four seasons share their harshness and ease; the three luminaries share their gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: The four seasons share their harshness and ease; the three luminaries share their gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 故身為之度，而聲為之律。

translations.literal: Therefore the body is their measure and the voice their pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the body is their measure and the voice their pitch.

sentences.zh: 勿謂無知，居高聽卑；

translations.literal: Do not say none know—high dwelling, low listening;
translations.idiomatic: Do not say none know—high dwelling, low listening;

sentences.zh: 勿謂何害，積小成大。

translations.literal: do not say what harm—small accumulates to great.
translations.idiomatic: do not say what harm—small accumulates to great.

sentences.zh: 樂不可極，極樂生哀；

translations.literal: Joy cannot be extreme; extreme joy begets sorrow;
translations.idiomatic: Joy cannot be extreme; extreme joy begets sorrow;

sentences.zh: 欲不可縱，縱欲成災。

translations.literal: desire cannot be indulged; indulged desire becomes disaster.
translations.idiomatic: desire cannot be indulged; indulged desire becomes disaster.

sentences.zh: 壯九重於內，所居不過容膝；

translations.literal: Magnifying the nine layers within—what one dwells in does not exceed room for the knees;
translations.idiomatic: Magnifying the nine layers within—what one dwells in does not exceed room for the knees;

sentences.zh: 彼昏不知，瑤其臺而瓊其室。

translations.literal: those benighted do not know, jade their towers and kingfisher their chambers.
translations.idiomatic: those benighted do not know, jade their towers and kingfisher their chambers.

sentences.zh: 羅八品於前，所食不過適口；

translations.literal: Spreading the eight ranks before one—what one eats does not exceed what suits the mouth;
translations.idiomatic: Spreading the eight ranks before one—what one eats does not exceed what suits the mouth;

sentences.zh: 唯狂罔念，丘其糟而池其酒。

translations.literal: only the mad forget, hill their dregs and pool their wine.
translations.idiomatic: only the mad forget, hill their dregs and pool their wine.

sentences.zh: 勿內荒於色，勿外荒於禽，勿貴難得之貨，勿聽亡國之音。

translations.literal: Do not be wild within with colors; do not be wild without with birds; do not prize hard-to-obtain goods; do not listen to music that destroys states.
translations.idiomatic: Do not be wild within with colors; do not be wild without with birds; do not prize hard-to-obtain goods; do not listen to music that destroys states.

sentences.zh: 內荒伐人性，外荒蕩人心，難得之貨侈，亡國之聲淫。

translations.literal: Wild within cuts down human nature; wild without unsettles human hearts; hard-to-obtain goods are extravagant; music that destroys states is licentious.
translations.idiomatic: Wild within cuts down human nature; wild without unsettles human hearts; hard-to-obtain goods are extravagant; music that destroys states is licentious.

sentences.zh: 勿謂我尊而傲賢侮士，勿謂我智而拒諫矜己。

translations.literal: Do not say I am honored and insult the worthy and humiliate scholars; do not say I am wise and reject remonstrance and pride oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Do not say I am honored and insult the worthy and humiliate scholars; do not say I am wise and reject remonstrance and pride oneself.

sentences.zh: 聞之夏王，據饋頻起；

translations.literal: One heard of the Xia king, rising repeatedly from the gift of food;
translations.idiomatic: One heard of the Xia king, rising repeatedly from the gift of food;

sentences.zh: 亦有魏帝，牽裾不止。

translations.literal: there was also the Wei emperor, tugging the robe without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: there was also the Wei emperor, tugging the robe without stopping.

sentences.zh: 安彼反側，如春陽秋露，巍巍蕩蕩，恢漢高大度；

translations.literal: Settling the contrary and perverse like spring sun and autumn dew; lofty and vast, restoring Han Gaozu's magnanimity;
translations.idiomatic: Settling the contrary and perverse like spring sun and autumn dew; lofty and vast, restoring Han Gaozu's magnanimity;

sentences.zh: 撫茲庶事，如履薄臨深，戰戰栗栗，用周文小心。

translations.literal: handling these many affairs as treading thin ice facing deep water, trembling and fearful, using King Wen of Zhou's carefulness.
translations.idiomatic: handling these many affairs as treading thin ice facing deep water, trembling and fearful, using King Wen of Zhou's carefulness.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「不識不知」，《書》曰：「無偏無黨」。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Without knowing, without knowing"; the Documents say: "Without partiality, without partisanship."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Without knowing, without knowing"; the Documents say, "Without partiality, without partisanship."

sentences.zh: 一彼此於胸臆，捐好惡於心想。

translations.literal: Casting this and that from the breast, casting likes and dislikes from thought.
translations.idiomatic: Casting this and that from the breast, casting likes and dislikes from thought.

sentences.zh: 眾棄而後加刑，眾悅而後命賞。

translations.literal: After the multitude abandons, then add punishment; after the multitude delights, then command reward.
translations.idiomatic: After the multitude abandons, then add punishment; after the multitude delights, then command reward.

sentences.zh: 弱其強而治其亂，申其屈而直其枉。

translations.literal: Weakening the strong and ordering the chaotic, extending the bent and straightening the crooked.
translations.idiomatic: Weakening the strong and ordering the chaotic, extending the bent and straightening the crooked.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「如衡如石，不定物以數，物之懸者，輕重自具；

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "Like balance like stone—not fixing things by number; what things hang from, light and heavy supply themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said, "Like balance like stone—not fixing things by number; what things hang from, light and heavy supply themselves;

sentences.zh: 如水如鏡，不示物以情，物之鑒者，妍媸自生。」

translations.literal: like water like mirror—not showing things feeling; what things reflect in, beauty and ugliness arise of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: like water like mirror—not showing things feeling; what things reflect in, beauty and ugliness arise of themselves."

sentences.zh: 勿渾渾而濁，勿皎皎而清，勿沒沒而暗，勿察察而明。

translations.literal: Do not be turbidly muddy; do not be brightly clear; do not be dimly dark; do not be keenly bright.
translations.idiomatic: Do not be turbidly muddy; do not be brightly clear; do not be dimly dark; do not be keenly bright.

sentences.zh: 雖冕旒蔽目而視於未形，雖黈纊塞耳而聽於無聲。

translations.literal: Though the tassels cover the eyes one sees what has no form; though the cotton plug stops the ears one hears what has no sound.
translations.idiomatic: Though the tassels cover the eyes one sees what has no form; though the cotton plug stops the ears one hears what has no sound.

sentences.zh: 縱心乎湛然之域，遊神於至道之精。

translations.literal: Release the heart in the realm of deep clarity; roam the spirit in the essence of utmost Way.
translations.idiomatic: Release the heart in the realm of deep clarity; roam the spirit in the essence of utmost Way.

sentences.zh: 扣之者應洪纖而效響，酌之者隨深淺而皆盈。

translations.literal: Strike it and it responds to thick and fine with echo; ladle it and it follows deep and shallow all full.
translations.idiomatic: Strike it and it responds to thick and fine with echo; ladle it and it follows deep and shallow all full.

sentences.zh: 故曰：天之清，地之寧，王之貞。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: Heaven's clarity, earth's tranquility, the king's rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: Heaven's clarity, earth's tranquility, the king's rectitude.

sentences.zh: 四時不言而代序，萬物無為而受成。

translations.literal: The four seasons speak not yet seasons replace one another; the myriad things act not yet receive completion.
translations.idiomatic: The four seasons speak not yet seasons replace one another; the myriad things act not yet receive completion.

sentences.zh: 豈知帝有其力，而天下和平。

translations.literal: Who knows the emperor has his power yet the realm is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Who knows the emperor has his power yet the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 吾王撥亂，戡以智力，民懼其威，未懷其德。

translations.literal: Our king pacified disorder, conquering by intelligence and strength; the people feared his awesomeness, not yet cherishing his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Our king pacified disorder, conquering by intelligence and strength; the people feared his awesomeness, not yet cherishing his virtue.

sentences.zh: 我皇撫運，扇以淳風，民懷其始，未保其終。

translations.literal: Our emperor nurtures fortune, fanning pure wind; the people cherish the beginning, not yet securing the end.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor nurtures fortune, fanning pure wind; the people cherish the beginning, not yet securing the end.

sentences.zh: 爰述金鏡，窮神盡聖；

translations.literal: Therefore I recount the golden mirror, exhausting spirit and utmost sagehood;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I recount the golden mirror, exhausting spirit and utmost sagehood;

sentences.zh: 使人以心，應言以行。

translations.literal: using people with the heart, responding to words with deeds.
translations.idiomatic: using people with the heart, responding to words with deeds.

sentences.zh: 包括治體，抑揚詞令，天下為公，一人有慶。

translations.literal: Embracing governing principles, elevating and lowering words and orders; the realm is public, one man has blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Embracing governing principles, elevating and lowering words and orders; the realm is public, one man has blessing.

sentences.zh: 開羅起祝，援琴命詩，一日二日，念茲在茲。

translations.literal: Opening the net to raise a toast, taking up the zither to command poetry—day one day two, keep this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Opening the net to raise a toast, taking up the zither to command poetry—day one day two, keep this in mind.

sentences.zh: 唯人所召，自天祐之。

translations.literal: Only what men summon, from Heaven it is aided.
translations.idiomatic: Only what men summon, from Heaven it is aided.

sentences.zh: 爭臣司直，敢告前疑！

translations.literal: Remonstrating ministers and upright officers dare report prior doubts!
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating ministers and upright officers dare report prior doubts!

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，賜以束帛，除大理丞。

translations.literal: Taizong commended it and granted silk; he was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong commended it and granted silk; he was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 初，河內人李孝德，素有風疾，而語涉妄妖。

translations.literal: Initially Li Xiaode of Henei had long had wind illness and his speech touched on wild sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Li Xiaode of Henei had long had wind illness and his speech touched on wild sorcery.

sentences.zh: 蘊古究其獄，稱好德癲病有征，法不當坐。

translations.literal: Yungu investigated his case and said Xiaode's mad illness had symptoms; by law he should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yungu investigated his case and said Xiaode's mad illness had symptoms; by law he should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史權萬紀劾蘊古家住相州，好德之兄厚德為其刺史，情在阿縱，奏事不實。

translations.literal: Drafting Secretary Quan Wanji impeached Yungu: his home was in Xiang Prefecture, Xiaode's elder brother Houde was its prefect—favor inclined to partiality, the memorial was not true.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Secretary Quan Wanji impeached Yungu: his home was in Xiang Prefecture, Xiaode's elder brother Houde was its prefect—favor inclined to partiality, the memorial was not true.

sentences.zh: 太宗大怒，曰：「小子乃敢亂吾法耶？」

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly angered and said: "This stripling dares to disturb my law!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was greatly angered and said, "This stripling dares to disturb my law!"

sentences.zh: 令斬於東市。

translations.literal: He ordered execution at the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered execution at the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 太宗尋悔，因發制，凡決死者，命所司五覆奏，自蘊古始也。

translations.literal: Taizong soon repented and therefore issued an edict: for all condemned to death, the responsible office must five times re-memorialize—beginning with Yungu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong soon repented and therefore issued an edict: for all condemned to death, the responsible office must five times re-memorialize—beginning with Yungu.

sentences.zh: 劉胤之

translations.literal: Liu Yinshi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yinshi

sentences.zh: 劉胤之，徐州彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yinshi was a man of Pengcheng in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yinshi was a man of Pengcheng in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖祎之，後魏臨淮鎮將。

translations.literal: Grandfather Yizhi, Garrison Commander of Linhuai of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Yizhi, Garrison Commander of Linhuai of Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 胤之少有學業，與隋信都丞孫萬壽、宗正卿李百藥為忘年之友。

translations.literal: Yinshi in youth had scholarship and with Sui's Assistant Administrator of Xindu Sun Wanshou and Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan Li Baiyao was a friend across the years.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshi in youth had scholarship and with Sui's Assistant Administrator of Xindu Sun Wanshou and Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan Li Baiyao was a friend across the years.

sentences.zh: 武德中，御史大夫杜淹表薦之，再遷信都令，甚存惠政。

translations.literal: In the Wude era Censor-in-Chief Du Yan memorialized recommending him; he was twice promoted to Magistrate of Xindu and greatly preserved benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era Censor-in-Chief Du Yan memorialized recommending him; he was twice promoted to Magistrate of Xindu and greatly preserved benevolent government.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，累轉著作郎、弘文館學士，與國子祭酒令狐德棻、著作郎楊仁卿等，撰成國史及實錄，奏上之，封陽城縣男。

translations.literal: In the early Yonghui era he was repeatedly transferred to Drafting Clerk of the Palace Library and Academic Scholar of the Hongwen Hall; with Guozi Jijiu Linghu Defen and Drafting Clerk Yang Renqing and others he completed the national history and veritable records, submitted them, and was enfeoffed Baron of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yonghui era he was repeatedly transferred to Drafting Clerk of the Palace Library and Academic Scholar of the Hongwen Hall; with Guozi Jijiu Linghu Defen and Drafting Clerk Yang Renqing and others he completed the national history and veritable records, submitted them, and was enfeoffed Baron of Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 尋以老，不堪著述，出為楚州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Soon because of age he could not bear compilation work, he was sent out as Prefect of Chu and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon because of age he could not bear compilation work, he was sent out as Prefect of Chu and died.

sentences.zh: 從子 延祐

translations.literal: Nephew Yanyou
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Yanyou

sentences.zh: 弟子延祐，弱冠本州舉進士，累補渭南尉。

translations.literal: Nephew Yanyou at weak crown was recommended as Jinshi in his home prefecture and repeatedly served as Assistant Magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Yanyou at weak crown was recommended as Jinshi in his home prefecture and repeatedly served as Assistant Magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 刀筆吏能，為畿邑當時之冠。

translations.literal: As a clerk with brush he had ability and was the crown of the capital districts of the time.
translations.idiomatic: As a clerk with brush he had ability and was the crown of the capital districts of the time.

sentences.zh: 司空李勣嘗謂曰：「足下春秋甫爾，便擅大名，宜稍自貶抑，無為獨出人右也。」

translations.literal: Minister of Works Li Ji once said to him: "Your grace is barely grown yet you monopolize great fame—you should slightly restrain yourself and not stand alone above others."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Li Ji once said to him, "Your grace is barely grown yet you monopolize great fame—you should slightly restrain yourself and not stand alone above others."

sentences.zh: 後歷右司郎中，檢校司賓少卿，封薛縣男。

translations.literal: Later he served as Director in the Ministry of Justice, Acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was enfeoffed Baron of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Director in the Ministry of Justice, Acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was enfeoffed Baron of Xue.

sentences.zh: 徐敬業之亂，揚州初平，所有刑名，莫能決定，延祐奉使至軍所決之。

translations.literal: In the disorder of Xu Jingye, when Yang Prefecture was first pacified, of all criminal cases none could be decided; Yanyou was sent as envoy to the army camp to decide them.
translations.idiomatic: In the disorder of Xu Jingye, when Yang Prefecture was first pacified, of all criminal cases none could be decided; Yanyou was sent as envoy to the army camp to decide them.

sentences.zh: 時議者斷受賊五品官者斬，六品者流。

translations.literal: At the time debaters judged those who accepted fifth-rank offices from the rebels should be beheaded, sixth-rank exiled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time debaters judged those who accepted fifth-rank offices from the rebels should be beheaded, sixth-rank exiled.

sentences.zh: 延祐以為諸非元謀，迫脅從盜，則置極刑，事涉枉濫，乃斷受賊五品者流，六品已下俱除名而已。

translations.literal: Yanyou considered that all who were not original plotters but were coerced to follow the bandits—if extreme punishment were applied the matter would involve wrongful excess; therefore he judged fifth-rank acceptors exiled, sixth-rank and below merely stripped of name.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyou considered that all who were not original plotters but were coerced to follow the bandits—if extreme punishment were applied the matter would involve wrongful excess; therefore he judged fifth-rank acceptors exiled, sixth-rank and below merely stripped of name.

sentences.zh: 其得全濟者甚眾。

translations.literal: Those fully spared were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Those fully spared were very many.

sentences.zh: 出為箕州刺史，轉安南都護。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Prefect of Ji and transferred to Protector-General of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Prefect of Ji and transferred to Protector-General of Annan.

sentences.zh: 嶺南俚戶，舊輸半課，及延祐到，遂勒全輸。

translations.literal: The Liao households of Lingnan originally paid half tax; when Yanyou arrived he compelled full payment.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao households of Lingnan originally paid half tax; when Yanyou arrived he compelled full payment.

sentences.zh: 由是其下皆怨，謀欲將叛，延祐乃誅其首惡李嗣仙。

translations.literal: On this account his subordinates all resented him and plotted rebellion; Yanyou then executed the ringleader Li Sixian.
translations.idiomatic: On this account his subordinates all resented him and plotted rebellion; Yanyou then executed the ringleader Li Sixian.

sentences.zh: 垂拱三年，嗣仙黨與丁建、李思慎等，遂率眾圍安南府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chuigong, Sixian's partisans Ding Jian, Li Sizhen, and others then led crowds to surround the Annan headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chuigong, Sixian's partisans Ding Jian, Li Sizhen, and others then led crowds to surround the Annan headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時城中勝兵不過數百，乃禁門堅守，以候鄰境之援。

translations.literal: At the time able soldiers in the city were no more than several hundred; they closed the gates and held firm, waiting for aid from neighboring territories.
translations.idiomatic: At the time able soldiers in the city were no more than several hundred; they closed the gates and held firm, waiting for aid from neighboring territories.

sentences.zh: 廣州大族馮子猷幸災樂禍，欲因危立功，遂按兵縱敵，使其為害滋甚。

translations.literal: Great clan leader of Guang Prefecture Feng Ziyou rejoiced in others' disaster and wished to exploit crisis to establish merit; he then held troops and released the enemy, letting harm grow greater.
translations.idiomatic: Great clan leader of Guang Prefecture Feng Ziyou rejoiced in others' disaster and wished to exploit crisis to establish merit; he then held troops and released the enemy, letting harm grow greater.

sentences.zh: 延祐遂為思慎所害。

translations.literal: Yanyou was then killed by Sizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyou was then killed by Sizhen.

sentences.zh: 其後桂州司馬曹玄靜率兵討思慎等，擒之。

translations.literal: Afterward Assistant Administrator of Gui Prefecture Cao Xuanjing led troops to attack Sizhen and others and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Assistant Administrator of Gui Prefecture Cao Xuanjing led troops to attack Sizhen and others and captured them.

sentences.zh: 盡斬於安南城下。

translations.literal: All were beheaded below the walls of Annan city.
translations.idiomatic: All were beheaded below the walls of Annan city.

sentences.zh: 從父兄子 藏器

translations.literal: Son of elder paternal cousin Zangqi
translations.idiomatic: Son of elder paternal cousin Zangqi

sentences.zh: 胤之從父兄子藏器，亦有詞學，官至宋州司馬。

translations.literal: Yinshi's son of elder paternal cousin Zangqi also had literary learning and reached Assistant Administrator of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshi's son of elder paternal cousin Zangqi also had literary learning and reached Assistant Administrator of Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 藏器子知柔，開元初，為工部尚書。

translations.literal: Zangqi's son Zhirou, in the early Kaiyuan era, was Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zangqi's son Zhirou, in the early Kaiyuan era, was Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 知柔弟知幾，避玄宗名改子玄。

translations.literal: Zhirou's younger brother Zhiji, avoiding Xuanzong's name, changed to Zixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou's younger brother Zhiji, avoiding Xuanzong's name, changed to Zixuan.

sentences.zh: 自有傳。

translations.literal: He has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: He has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 張昌齡

translations.literal: Zhang Changling
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changling

sentences.zh: 張昌齡，冀州南宮人。

translations.literal: Zhang Changling was a man of Nangong in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changling was a man of Nangong in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弱冠以文詞知名。

translations.literal: At weak crown he was renowned for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: At weak crown he was renowned for literary composition.

sentences.zh: 本州欲以秀才舉之，昌齡以時廢此科已久，固辭。

translations.literal: His home prefecture wished to recommend him as Xiucai; Changling considered this category long abolished and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: His home prefecture wished to recommend him as Xiucai; Changling considered this category long abolished and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 乃充進士貢舉及第。

translations.literal: He then entered as Jinshi tribute candidate and passed.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered as Jinshi tribute candidate and passed.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十一年，翠微宮成，詣闕獻頌。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan, when Cuiwei Palace was completed, he went to the gate and presented a eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan, when Cuiwei Palace was completed, he went to the gate and presented a eulogy.

sentences.zh: 太宗召見，試作《息兵詔》草，俄頃而就。

translations.literal: Taizong summoned him and tested him composing a draft Cease Arms Edict; in a moment it was done.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned him and tested him composing a draft Cease Arms Edict; in a moment it was done.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚悅，因謂之曰：「昔禰衡、潘嶽，皆恃才傲物，以至非命。

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly pleased and said to him: "Formerly Mi Heng and Pan Yue both relied on talent and were arrogant toward others, until they met untimely death.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was greatly pleased and said to him, "Formerly Mi Heng and Pan Yue both relied on talent and were arrogant toward others, until they met untimely death.

sentences.zh: 汝才不減二賢，宜追鑒前軌，以副吾所取也。」

translations.literal: Your talent is not inferior to those two worthies—you should follow the earlier track to match what I have chosen of you."
translations.idiomatic: Your talent is not inferior to those two worthies—you should follow the earlier track to match what I have chosen of you."

sentences.zh: 乃敕於通事舍人裏供奉。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered him to attend within the office of the Herald.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered him to attend within the office of the Herald.

sentences.zh: 尋為昆山道行軍記室，破盧明月，平龜茲，軍書露布，皆昌齡之文也。

translations.literal: Soon he was Army Recorder on the Kunshan Circuit, defeating Lu Mingyue and pacifying Kucha—all military documents and victory bulletins were Changling's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Army Recorder on the Kunshan Circuit, defeating Lu Mingyue and pacifying Kucha—all military documents and victory bulletins were Changling's writing.

sentences.zh: 再轉長安尉，出為襄州司戶，丁憂去官。

translations.literal: He was twice transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Chang'an and sent out as Revenue Clerk of Xiang Prefecture; he left office on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Chang'an and sent out as Revenue Clerk of Xiang Prefecture; he left office on mourning.

sentences.zh: 後賀蘭敏之奏引於北門修撰，尋又罷去。

translations.literal: Later Helan Minzhi memorialized recommending him for compilation at the North Gate; soon he was again dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Helan Minzhi memorialized recommending him for compilation at the North Gate; soon he was again dismissed.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianfeng he died.

sentences.zh: 文集二十卷。

translations.literal: Collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 兄 昌宗

translations.literal: Elder brother Changzong
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Changzong

sentences.zh: 兄昌宗，亦有學業，官至太子舍人、修文館學士。

translations.literal: Elder brother Changzong also had scholarship and reached Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Academic Scholar of the Hall of Cultivated Letters.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Changzong also had scholarship and reached Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Academic Scholar of the Hall of Cultivated Letters.

sentences.zh: 撰《古文紀年新傳》三十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled the New Chronicle of Ancient Writing in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the New Chronicle of Ancient Writing in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 崔行功

translations.literal: Cui Xinggong
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xinggong

sentences.zh: 崔行功，恆州井陘人，北齊鉅鹿太守伯讓曾孫也，自博陵徙家焉。

translations.literal: Cui Xinggong was a man of Jingxing in Heng Prefecture, great-grandson of Boyang, Prefect of Julu of Northern Qi; his family moved there from Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xinggong was a man of Jingxing in Heng Prefecture, great-grandson of Boyang, Prefect of Julu of Northern Qi; his family moved there from Boling.

sentences.zh: 行功少好學，中書侍郎唐儉愛其才，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Xinggong in youth loved learning; Vice Director of the Secretariat Tang Jian loved his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong in youth loved learning; Vice Director of the Secretariat Tang Jian loved his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 儉前後征討，所有文表，皆行功之文。

translations.literal: In Jian's successive campaigns all documents and memorials were Xinggong's writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian's successive campaigns all documents and memorials were Xinggong's writing.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，累轉吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以善敷奏，嘗兼通事舍人、內供奉。

translations.literal: Because he was skilled at memorializing, he once concurrently served as Herald and inner attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was skilled at memorializing, he once concurrently served as Herald and inner attendant.

sentences.zh: 坐事貶為遊安令，尋征為司文郎中。

translations.literal: Punished for an offense he was demoted Magistrate of You'an; soon he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for an offense he was demoted Magistrate of You'an; soon he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 當時朝廷大手筆，多是行功及蘭臺侍郎李懷儼之詞。

translations.literal: At the time the court's great brushwork was mostly the words of Xinggong and Vice Director of the Orchid Terrace Li Huaiyan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court's great brushwork was mostly the words of Xinggong and Vice Director of the Orchid Terrace Li Huaiyan.

sentences.zh: 先是，太宗命秘書監魏征寫四部群書，將進內貯庫，別置讎校二十人、書手一百人。

translations.literal: Previously Taizong ordered Secretariat Director Wei Zheng to copy the four categories of books to be stored in the inner treasury, separately setting twenty collators and one hundred copyists.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Taizong ordered Secretariat Director Wei Zheng to copy the four categories of books to be stored in the inner treasury, separately setting twenty collators and one hundred copyists.

sentences.zh: 征改職之後，令虞世南、顏師古等續其事。

translations.literal: After Zheng changed posts, he ordered Yu Shinan, Yan Shigu, and others to continue the work.
translations.idiomatic: After Zheng changed posts, he ordered Yu Shinan, Yan Shigu, and others to continue the work.

sentences.zh: 至高宗初，其功未畢。

translations.literal: By the early Gaozong era the work was not yet finished.
translations.idiomatic: By the early Gaozong era the work was not yet finished.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，罷讎校及御書手，令工書人繕寫，計直酬傭，擇散官隨番讎校。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era collators and imperial copyists were abolished; skilled copyists were ordered to transcribe, calculating payment by piecework, selecting unattached officials to collate in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianqing era collators and imperial copyists were abolished; skilled copyists were ordered to transcribe, calculating payment by piecework, selecting unattached officials to collate in rotation.

sentences.zh: 其後又詔東臺侍郎趙仁本、東臺舍人張文瓘及行功、懷儼等相次充使檢校。

translations.literal: Afterward an edict also ordered Vice Director of the Eastern Terrace Zhao Renben, Attendant of the Eastern Terrace Zhang Wenwan, and Xinggong and Huaiyan and others to serve successively as inspection commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward an edict also ordered Vice Director of the Eastern Terrace Zhao Renben, Attendant of the Eastern Terrace Zhang Wenwan, and Xinggong and Huaiyan and others to serve successively as inspection commissioners.

sentences.zh: 又置詳正學士以校理之，行功仍專知御集。

translations.literal: Detailed collation scholars were also set up to collate and order; Xinggong still specially managed the imperial collection.
translations.idiomatic: Detailed collation scholars were also set up to collate and order; Xinggong still specially managed the imperial collection.

sentences.zh: 遷蘭臺侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted Vice Director of the Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Vice Director of the Orchid Terrace.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，官名復舊，改為秘書少監。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng era official titles were restored to the old; he was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianheng era official titles were restored to the old; he was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan he died in office.

sentences.zh: 有集六十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection in sixty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collection in sixty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 兄子玄暐，別有傳。

translations.literal: Nephew son Xuanhui has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew son Xuanhui has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 行功前後預撰《晉書》及《文思博要》等。

translations.literal: Xinggong before and after participated in compiling the History of Jin and the Comprehensive Digest of Literary Thought and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong before and after participated in compiling the History of Jin and the Comprehensive Digest of Literary Thought and others.

sentences.zh: 同時又有孟利貞、董思恭、元思敬等，並以文藻知名。

translations.literal: At the same time there were also Meng Lizhen, Dong Sigong, Yuan Sijing, and others—all renowned for literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there were also Meng Lizhen, Dong Sigong, Yuan Sijing, and others—all renowned for literary ornament.

sentences.zh: 附 孟利貞

translations.literal: Appended: Meng Lizhen
translations.idiomatic: Appended: Meng Lizhen

sentences.zh: 孟利貞者，華州華陰人也。

translations.literal: Meng Lizhen was a man of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Lizhen was a man of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父神慶，高宗初為沁州刺史，以清介著名。

translations.literal: Father Shenqing, in the early Gaozong era was Prefect of Qin Prefecture, famed for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Father Shenqing, in the early Gaozong era was Prefect of Qin Prefecture, famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 利貞初為太子司議郎，中宗在東宮，深懼之。

translations.literal: Lizhen initially was Remonstrator of the Heir Apparent; when Zhongzong was in the Eastern Palace he deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen initially was Remonstrator of the Heir Apparent; when Zhongzong was in the Eastern Palace he deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 受詔與少師許敬宗、崇賢館學士郭瑜、顧胤、董思恭等撰《瑤山玉彩》五百卷。

translations.literal: Receiving an edict with Junior Tutor Xu Jingzong and Academic Scholars of the Hall of Honoring the Worthy Guo Yu, Gu Yin, and Dong Sigong and others he compiled the Jade Splendor of Mount Yao in five hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving an edict with Junior Tutor Xu Jingzong and Academic Scholars of the Hall of Honoring the Worthy Guo Yu, Gu Yin, and Dong Sigong and others he compiled the Jade Splendor of Mount Yao in five hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年奏上之，高宗稱善，加級賜物有差。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo it was submitted; Gaozong praised it and added rank and granted goods in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo it was submitted; Gaozong praised it and added rank and granted goods in differing amounts.

sentences.zh: 利貞累轉著作郎，加弘文館學士。

translations.literal: Lizhen was repeatedly transferred to Drafting Clerk and added Academic Scholar of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen was repeatedly transferred to Drafting Clerk and added Academic Scholar of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初卒。

translations.literal: In the early Chuigong era he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chuigong era he died.

sentences.zh: 又撰《續文選》十三卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled the Continuation of the Literary Selection in thirteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Continuation of the Literary Selection in thirteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 兄 允忠

translations.literal: Elder brother Yongzhong
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Yongzhong

sentences.zh: 兄允忠，垂拱中為天官侍郎。

translations.literal: Elder brother Yongzhong, in the Chuigong era was Vice Director of the Celestial Office.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Yongzhong, in the Chuigong era was Vice Director of the Celestial Office.

sentences.zh: 附 董思恭

translations.literal: Appended: Dong Sigong
translations.idiomatic: Appended: Dong Sigong

sentences.zh: 董思恭者，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Dong Sigong was a man of Wu in Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Sigong was a man of Wu in Su Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 所著篇詠，甚為時人所重。

translations.literal: The compositions he authored were greatly valued by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: The compositions he authored were greatly valued by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 初為右史，知考功舉事，坐預泄問目，配流嶺表而死。

translations.literal: Initially he was Right Historian, knowing examination affairs; punished for leaking questions he was exiled to Lingnan and died.
translations.idiomatic: Initially he was Right Historian, knowing examination affairs; punished for leaking questions he was exiled to Lingnan and died.

sentences.zh: 附 元思敬

translations.literal: Appended: Yuan Sijing
translations.idiomatic: Appended: Yuan Sijing

sentences.zh: 元思敬者，總章中為協律郎。

translations.literal: Yuan Sijing, in the Zongzhang era was Director of Harmonizing Music.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Sijing, in the Zongzhang era was Director of Harmonizing Music.

sentences.zh: 預修《芳林要覽》，又撰《詩人秀句》兩卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the Forest Compendium of Excellence and also compiled Poets' Fine Lines in two scrolls, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He participated in compiling the Forest Compendium of Excellence and also compiled Poets' Fine Lines in two scrolls, transmitted in the world.

sentences.zh: 徐齊聃

translations.literal: Xu Qipan
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qipan

sentences.zh: 徐齊聃，湖州長城人也。

translations.literal: Xu Qipan was a man of Changcheng in Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qipan was a man of Changcheng in Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父孝德，以女為才人，官至果州刺史。

translations.literal: Father Xiaode, because his daughter was a Talented Lady, reached Prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Father Xiaode, because his daughter was a Talented Lady, reached Prefect of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊聃少善屬文，高宗時累遷蘭臺舍人。

translations.literal: Qipan in youth was skilled at literary composition; under Gaozong he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Qipan in youth was skilled at literary composition; under Gaozong he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Orchid Terrace.

sentences.zh: 時敕令有突厥酋長子弟事東宮，齊聃上疏曰：

translations.literal: At the time an edict concerned sons of Turkic chieftains serving the Eastern Palace; Qipan submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: At the time an edict concerned sons of Turkic chieftains serving the Eastern Palace; Qipan submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 昔姬誦與伯禽同業，晉儲以師曠為友，匪唯專賴師資，固亦詳觀近習。

translations.literal: Formerly Prince Song of Zhou studied with Bo Qin; the Heir Apparent of Jin took Music Master Kuang as friend—not only relying specially on teachers, but also closely observing near companions.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Prince Song of Zhou studied with Bo Qin; the Heir Apparent of Jin took Music Master Kuang as friend—not only relying specially on teachers, but also closely observing near companions.

sentences.zh: 皇太子自可招集園、綺，寤寐應、劉。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent may naturally summon Yuan and Qi, waking and sleeping with Ying and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent may naturally summon Yuan and Qi, waking and sleeping with Ying and Liu.

sentences.zh: 階闥小臣，必采於端士；

translations.literal: Petty ministers at the gate must be chosen from upright gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: Petty ministers at the gate must be chosen from upright gentlemen;

sentences.zh: 驅馳所任，並歸於正人。

translations.literal: those charged to attend must all be returned to proper men.
translations.idiomatic: those charged to attend must all be returned to proper men.

sentences.zh: 方流好善之風，永播崇賢之美。

translations.literal: Then will flow the wind of loving goodness and forever spread the beauty of honoring the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Then will flow the wind of loving goodness and forever spread the beauty of honoring the worthy.

sentences.zh: 今乃使氈裘之子，解辮而侍春闈；

translations.literal: Now sons in felt robes are made to unbraid hair and attend the spring gate;
translations.idiomatic: Now sons in felt robes are made to unbraid hair and attend the spring gate;

sentences.zh: 冒頓之苗，削袵而陪望苑。

translations.literal: seed of Modu, cutting robes, accompany the lookout garden.
translations.idiomatic: seed of Modu, cutting robes, accompany the lookout garden.

sentences.zh: 在於道義，臣竊有疑。

translations.literal: In point of moral principle, your subject privately has doubts.
translations.idiomatic: In point of moral principle, your subject privately has doubts.

sentences.zh: 詩云：「敬慎威儀，以近有德。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Reverent and cautious in dignity, to draw near to the virtuous."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Reverent and cautious in dignity, to draw near to the virtuous."

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「任官惟賢才，左右惟其人。」

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Appoint officials only for talent and ability; attendants left and right only for their persons."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, "Appoint officials only for talent and ability; attendants left and right only for their persons."

sentences.zh: 蓋殷勤於此，防微之至也。

translations.literal: Truly earnestness here—to the utmost in guarding against the subtle.
translations.idiomatic: Truly earnestness here—to the utmost in guarding against the subtle.

sentences.zh: 齊聃又嘗上奏曰：「齊獻公即陛下外氏，雖子孫有犯，不合上延於祖。

translations.literal: Qipan also once submitted a memorial saying: "Duke Zhongxiao of Qi is Your Majesty's maternal clan; though descendants may offend, it is not fitting to extend upward to ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Qipan also once submitted a memorial saying, "Duke Zhongxiao of Qi is Your Majesty's maternal clan; though descendants may offend, it is not fitting to extend upward to ancestors.

sentences.zh: 今周忠孝公廟甚修崇，而齊獻公廟遽毀壞，不審陛下將何以重示海內，以彰孝理之風？」

translations.literal: Now the temple of Duke Zhongxiao of Zhou is greatly repaired while the temple of Duke Zhongxiao of Qi was suddenly destroyed—I do not know how Your Majesty will heavily show the realm and manifest the wind of filial principle?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the temple of Duke Zhongxiao of Zhou is greatly repaired while the temple of Duke Zhongxiao of Qi was suddenly destroyed—I do not know how Your Majesty will heavily show the realm and manifest the wind of filial principle?"

sentences.zh: 帝皆納其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted both statements.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted both statements.

sentences.zh: 齊聃善於文誥，甚為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Qipan was skilled at documents and edicts and was greatly praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Qipan was skilled at documents and edicts and was greatly praised by the age.

sentences.zh: 高宗愛其文，令侍周王等屬文，以職在樞劇，仍敕間日來往焉。

translations.literal: Gaozong loved his writing and ordered him to assist the Prince of Zhou and others in composition; because his duties were in urgent secret matters, he was still ordered to come and go on alternate days.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong loved his writing and ordered him to assist the Prince of Zhou and others in composition; because his duties were in urgent secret matters, he was still ordered to come and go on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 以漏泄機密，左授蘄州司馬。

translations.literal: For leaking secrets he was demoted left to Assistant Administrator of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For leaking secrets he was demoted left to Assistant Administrator of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄又坐事配流欽州。

translations.literal: Soon he was again punished and exiled to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again punished and exiled to Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中卒，年四十余。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng era he died, aged over forty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianheng era he died, aged over forty.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，追錄舊恩，累贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne he traced old favor and repeatedly posthumously promoted him to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne he traced old favor and repeatedly posthumously promoted him to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子堅，別有傳。

translations.literal: Son Jian has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Son Jian has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 杜易簡

translations.literal: Du Yijian
translations.idiomatic: Du Yijian

sentences.zh: 杜易簡，襄州襄陽人，周硤州刺史叔毗曾孫也。

translations.literal: Du Yijian was a man of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture, great-grandson of Shubi, Prefect of Xia of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yijian was a man of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture, great-grandson of Shubi, Prefect of Xia of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 九歲能屬文，及長，博學有高名。

translations.literal: At nine sui he could compose text; when grown he was broadly learned and had high fame.
translations.idiomatic: At nine sui he could compose text; when grown he was broadly learned and had high fame.

sentences.zh: 姨兄中書令岑文本甚推重之。

translations.literal: Maternal cousin by marriage Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Maternal cousin by marriage Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben greatly esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，累轉殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He passed the Jinshi examination and was repeatedly transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Jinshi examination and was repeatedly transferred to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，為考功員外郎。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng era he was Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianheng era he was Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時吏部侍郎裴行儉、李敬玄相與不葉，易簡與吏部員外郎賈言忠希行儉之旨，上封陳敬玄罪狀。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Director of Personnel Pei Xingjian and Li Jingxuan were mutually at odds; Yijian with Vice Director Jia Yanzhong hoped for Xingjian's intent and submitted a sealed memorial stating Jingxuan's offenses.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Vice Director of Personnel Pei Xingjian and Li Jingxuan were mutually at odds; Yijian with Vice Director Jia Yanzhong hoped for Xingjian's intent and submitted a sealed memorial stating Jingxuan's offenses.

sentences.zh: 高宗惡其朋黨，左轉易簡為開州司馬，尋卒。

translations.literal: Gaozong hated their faction; Yijian was demoted left to Assistant Administrator of Kai Prefecture and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong hated their faction; Yijian was demoted left to Assistant Administrator of Kai Prefecture and soon died.

sentences.zh: 易簡頗善著述，撰《御史臺雜註》五卷，文集二十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: Yijian was quite skilled at writing and compiled Miscellaneous Notes of the Censorate in five scrolls and collected works in twenty scrolls, circulating in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian was quite skilled at writing and compiled Miscellaneous Notes of the Censorate in five scrolls and collected works in twenty scrolls, circulating in the age.

sentences.zh: 易簡從祖弟審言。

translations.literal: Yijian's younger paternal cousin of the same grandfather Shenyan.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian's younger paternal cousin of the same grandfather Shenyan.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟 審言

translations.literal: Younger paternal cousin of the same grandfather Shenyan
translations.idiomatic: Younger paternal cousin of the same grandfather Shenyan

sentences.zh: 審言，進士舉，初為隰城尉。

translations.literal: Shenyan, recommended as Jinshi, initially was Assistant Magistrate of Yincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyan, recommended as Jinshi, initially was Assistant Magistrate of Yincheng.

sentences.zh: 雅善五言詩，工書翰，有能名。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at five-character poetry and skilled at calligraphy, with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at five-character poetry and skilled at calligraphy, with a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 然恃才謇傲，甚為時輩所嫉。

translations.literal: Yet relying on talent he was blunt and arrogant and was greatly envied by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yet relying on talent he was blunt and arrogant and was greatly envied by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 乾封中，蘇味道為天官侍郎，審言預選。

translations.literal: In the Qianfeng era Su Weidao was Vice Director of the Celestial Office; Shenyan participated in selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfeng era Su Weidao was Vice Director of the Celestial Office; Shenyan participated in selection.

sentences.zh: 試判訖，謂人曰：「蘇味道必死。」

translations.literal: When the examination judgment was finished he said to people: "Su Weidao must die."
translations.idiomatic: When the examination judgment was finished he said to people, "Su Weidao must die."

sentences.zh: 人問其故，審言曰：「見吾判，即自當羞死矣！」

translations.literal: People asked the reason; Shenyan said: "Seeing my judgment, he should die of shame!"
translations.idiomatic: People asked the reason; Shenyan said, "Seeing my judgment, he should die of shame!"

sentences.zh: 又嘗謂人曰：「吾之文章，合得屈、宋作衙官；

translations.literal: He also once said to people: "My literary compositions ought to have Qu and Song as yamen officers;
translations.idiomatic: He also once said to people, "My literary compositions ought to have Qu and Song as yamen officers;

sentences.zh: 吾之書跡，合得王羲之北面。」

translations.literal: my calligraphy ought to have Wang Xizhi face north."
translations.idiomatic: my calligraphy ought to have Wang Xizhi face north."

sentences.zh: 其矜誕如此。

translations.literal: His arrogance and extravagance were thus.
translations.idiomatic: His arrogance and extravagance were thus.

sentences.zh: 累轉洛陽丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 坐事貶授吉州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Punished for an offense he was demoted and appointed Revenue Clerk of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for an offense he was demoted and appointed Revenue Clerk of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又與州僚不葉，司馬周季重與員外司戶郭若訥共構審言罪狀，繫獄，將因事殺之。

translations.literal: Again at odds with prefectural colleagues, Assistant Administrator Zhou Jizhong with Outer Revenue Clerk Guo Ruone jointly framed charges against Shenyan and imprisoned him, intending to kill him on a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Again at odds with prefectural colleagues, Assistant Administrator Zhou Jizhong with Outer Revenue Clerk Guo Ruone jointly framed charges against Shenyan and imprisoned him, intending to kill him on a pretext.

sentences.zh: 既而季重等府中酣宴，審言子並年十三，懷刃以擊之。

translations.literal: Then Jizhong and others feasted deeply in the headquarters; Shenyan's son Bing, aged thirteen, concealed a blade and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jizhong and others feasted deeply in the headquarters; Shenyan's son Bing, aged thirteen, concealed a blade and struck them.

sentences.zh: 季重中傷死，而並亦為左右所殺。

translations.literal: Jizhong was wounded and died; Bing was also killed by attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong was wounded and died; Bing was also killed by attendants.

sentences.zh: 季重臨死曰：「吾不知審言有孝子，郭若訥誤我至此！」

translations.literal: Jizhong at death said: "I did not know Shenyan had a filial son—Guo Ruone misled me to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong at death said, "I did not know Shenyan had a filial son—Guo Ruone misled me to this!"

sentences.zh: 審言因此免官，還東都，自為文祭並。

translations.literal: Shenyan on this account was dismissed and returned to the eastern capital, himself composing a funeral text for Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyan on this account was dismissed and returned to the eastern capital, himself composing a funeral text for Bing.

sentences.zh: 士友鹹哀並孝烈，蘇颋為墓誌，劉允濟為祭文。

translations.literal: Scholars and friends all mourned Bing's filial heroism; Su Ting wrote his tomb inscription and Liu Yunji his funeral text.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and friends all mourned Bing's filial heroism; Su Ting wrote his tomb inscription and Liu Yunji his funeral text.

sentences.zh: 後則天召見審言，將加擢用。

translations.literal: Later Zetian summoned Shenyan intending to promote him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zetian summoned Shenyan intending to promote him.

sentences.zh: 問曰：「卿歡喜否？」

translations.literal: She asked: "Are you pleased?"
translations.idiomatic: She asked, "Are you pleased?"

sentences.zh: 審言蹈舞謝恩。

translations.literal: Shenyan danced in joy and thanked for grace.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyan danced in joy and thanked for grace.

sentences.zh: 因令作《歡喜詩》，甚見嘉賞，拜著作佐郎。

translations.literal: She then ordered him to compose the Joyful Poem; he was greatly praised and appointed Assistant Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: She then ordered him to compose the Joyful Poem; he was greatly praised and appointed Assistant Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 俄遷膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Vice Director in the Ministry of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted Vice Director in the Ministry of Provisions.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，坐與張易之兄弟交往，配流嶺外。

translations.literal: In the early Shenlong era, punished for associating with the Zhang Yizhi brothers, he was exiled beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shenlong era, punished for associating with the Zhang Yizhi brothers, he was exiled beyond the ranges.

sentences.zh: 尋召授國子監主簿，加修文館直學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Director of the Directorate of Education and added Direct Academic Scholar of the Hall of Cultivated Letters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned and appointed Director of the Directorate of Education and added Direct Academic Scholar of the Hall of Cultivated Letters.

sentences.zh: 年六十余卒。

translations.literal: Aged over sixty he died.
translations.idiomatic: Aged over sixty he died.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collected works in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 次子閑。

translations.literal: Second son Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Xian.

sentences.zh: 閑子甫，別有傳。

translations.literal: Xian's son Fu has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's son Fu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 盧照鄰

translations.literal: Lu Zhaolin
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhaolin

sentences.zh: 盧照鄰，字升之，幽州范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhaolin, styled Shengzhi, was a man of Fanyang in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhaolin, styled Shengzhi, was a man of Fanyang in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年十余歲，就曹憲、王義方授《蒼》、《雅》及經史，博學善屬文。

translations.literal: At over ten sui he studied the Cangjie and Erya lexicons and classics and histories under Cao Xian and Wang Yifang, broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: At over ten sui he studied the Cangjie and Erya lexicons and classics and histories under Cao Xian and Wang Yifang, broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 初授鄧王府典簽，王甚愛重之，曾謂群官曰：「此即寡人相如也。」

translations.literal: Initially appointed Record Keeper of the Prince of Deng's establishment; the prince greatly loved and valued him and once said to assembled officials: "This is my Sima Xiangru."
translations.idiomatic: Initially appointed Record Keeper of the Prince of Deng's establishment; the prince greatly loved and valued him and once said to assembled officials, "This is my Sima Xiangru."

sentences.zh: 後拜新都尉。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 因染風疾去官，處太白山中，以服餌為事。

translations.literal: Because he contracted wind illness he left office and dwelt in Mount Taibai, making diet and medicine his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Because he contracted wind illness he left office and dwelt in Mount Taibai, making diet and medicine his occupation.

sentences.zh: 後疾轉篤，徙居陽翟之具茨山，著《釋疾文》、《五悲》等誦。

translations.literal: Later the illness grew severe and he moved to Mount Juci of Yangdi, composing the Explanatory Essay on Illness and the Five Laments and other pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Later the illness grew severe and he moved to Mount Juci of Yangdi, composing the Explanatory Essay on Illness and the Five Laments and other pieces.

sentences.zh: 頗有騷人之風，甚為文士所重。

translations.literal: He quite had the flavor of a sao poet and was greatly valued by literary men.
translations.idiomatic: He quite had the flavor of a sao poet and was greatly valued by literary men.

sentences.zh: 照鄰既沈痼攣廢，不堪其苦，嘗與親屬執別，遂自投潁水而死，時年四十。

translations.literal: Zhaolin, sunk in chronic paralysis and crippled, could not bear the suffering; once taking leave of kin he threw himself into the Ying River and died, aged forty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin, sunk in chronic paralysis and crippled, could not bear the suffering; once taking leave of kin he threw himself into the Ying River and died, aged forty.

sentences.zh: 文集二十卷。

translations.literal: Collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 兄 光乘

translations.literal: Elder brother Guangcheng
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Guangcheng

sentences.zh: 兄光乘，亦知名，長壽中為隴州刺史。

translations.literal: Elder brother Guangcheng was also renowned and in the Changshou era was Prefect of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Guangcheng was also renowned and in the Changshou era was Prefect of Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 楊炯

translations.literal: Yang Jiong
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiong

sentences.zh: 楊炯，華陰人。

translations.literal: Yang Jiong was a man of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiong was a man of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 伯祖虔威，武德中官至右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Granduncle Qianwei, in the Wude era reached General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Granduncle Qianwei, in the Wude era reached General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 炯幼聰敏博學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Jiong in youth was clever, keen, and broadly learned, skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong in youth was clever, keen, and broadly learned, skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 神童舉，拜校書郎，為崇文館學士。

translations.literal: Recommended as child prodigy he was appointed Collator and Academic Scholar of the Hall of Cultivated Letters.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as child prodigy he was appointed Collator and Academic Scholar of the Hall of Cultivated Letters.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，太常博士蘇知幾上表，以公卿已下冕服，請別立節文。

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Su Zhiji submitted a memorial that from dukes and ministers downward court dress should have separate ritual texts.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yifeng era Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Su Zhiji submitted a memorial that from dukes and ministers downward court dress should have separate ritual texts.

sentences.zh: 敕下有司詳議，炯獻議曰：

translations.literal: An edict was issued ordering the relevant offices to deliberate in detail, and Jiong submitted a memorial arguing:
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued ordering the relevant offices to deliberate in detail, and Jiong submitted a memorial arguing:

sentences.zh: 由是竟寢知幾所請。

translations.literal: On this account Zhi Ji's request was ultimately shelved.
translations.idiomatic: On this account Zhi Ji's request was ultimately shelved.

sentences.zh: 俄遷詹事司直。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Direct Clerk of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted Direct Clerk of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 則天初，坐從祖弟神讓犯逆，左轉梓州司法參軍。

translations.literal: In the early Zetian era, punished because younger paternal cousin Shenrang committed treason, he was demoted left to Judicial Military Administrator of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zetian era, punished because younger paternal cousin Shenrang committed treason, he was demoted left to Judicial Military Administrator of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，選授盈川令。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was selected and appointed Magistrate of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was selected and appointed Magistrate of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 如意元年七月望日，宮中出盂蘭盆，分送佛寺，則天禦洛南門，與百僚觀之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ruyi, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the palace sent out Ullambana bowls to Buddhist temples; Zetian attended the south gate of Luoyang with the hundred officials to view them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ruyi, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the palace sent out Ullambana bowls to Buddhist temples; Zetian attended the south gate of Luoyang with the hundred officials to view them.

sentences.zh: 炯獻《盂蘭盆賦》，詞甚雅麗。

translations.literal: Jiong presented the Rhapsody on the Ullambana Bowl; the language was very elegant and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong presented the Rhapsody on the Ullambana Bowl; the language was very elegant and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 炯至官，為政殘酷，人吏動不如意，輒搒殺之。

translations.literal: When Jiong reached office his governance was cruel; when officials and clerks did not suit his wish he beat them to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong reached office his governance was cruel; when officials and clerks did not suit his wish he beat them to death.

sentences.zh: 又所居府舍，多進士亭臺，皆書榜額，為之美名，大為遠近所笑。

translations.literal: Also the official residence mostly had pavilions built by Jinshi candidates, all with inscribed placards making fine names—greatly laughed at by near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Also the official residence mostly had pavilions built by Jinshi candidates, all with inscribed placards making fine names—greatly laughed at by near and far.

sentences.zh: 無何卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，以舊僚追贈著作郎。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, as an old associate he was posthumously promoted Drafting Clerk of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, as an old associate he was posthumously promoted Drafting Clerk of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 文集三十卷。

translations.literal: Collected works in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Collected works in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 炯與王勃、盧照鄰、駱賓王以文詞齊名，海內稱為王楊盧駱，亦號為「四傑」。

translations.literal: Jiong with Wang Bo, Lu Zhaolin, and Luo Binwang were equally famed for literary composition; within the seas they were called Wang, Yang, Lu, and Luo, also styled the "Four Outstanding".
translations.idiomatic: Jiong with Wang Bo, Lu Zhaolin, and Luo Binwang were equally famed for literary composition; within the seas they were called Wang, Yang, Lu, and Luo, also styled the "Four Outstanding".

sentences.zh: 炯聞之，謂人曰：「吾愧在盧前，恥居王後。」

translations.literal: Jiong heard this and said to people: "I am ashamed to stand before Lu and shamed to stand after Wang."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong heard this and said to people, "I am ashamed to stand before Lu and shamed to stand after Wang."

sentences.zh: 當時議者，亦以為然。

translations.literal: Debaters of the time also considered it so.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters of the time also considered it so.

sentences.zh: 其後崔融、李嶠、張說俱重四傑之文。

translations.literal: Afterward Cui Rong, Li Jiao, and Zhang Yue all valued the Four Outstanding's writing.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Cui Rong, Li Jiao, and Zhang Yue all valued the Four Outstanding's writing.

sentences.zh: 崔融曰：「王勃文章宏逸，有絕塵之跡，固非常流所及。

translations.literal: Cui Rong said: "Wang Bo's writing is grand and swift, with traces of leaving the dust—truly not what ordinary streams reach.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rong said, "Wang Bo's writing is grand and swift, with traces of leaving the dust—truly not what ordinary streams reach.

sentences.zh: 炯與照鄰可以企之，盈川之言信矣！」

translations.literal: Jiong and Zhaolin can aspire to them; Yingchuan's words are true!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiong and Zhaolin can aspire to them; Yingchuan's words are true!"

sentences.zh: 說曰：「楊盈川文思如懸河註水，酌之不竭，既優於盧，亦不減王。

translations.literal: Yue said: "Yang Yingchuan's literary thought is like a suspended river pouring water—ladle without exhaustion; he is superior to Lu and not inferior to Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Yang Yingchuan's literary thought is like a suspended river pouring water—ladle without exhaustion; he is superior to Lu and not inferior to Wang.

sentences.zh: 『恥居王後』，信然；

translations.literal: 'Shamed to stand after Wang'—truly so;
translations.idiomatic: 'Shamed to stand after Wang'—truly so;

sentences.zh: 『愧在盧前』，謙也。」

translations.literal: Ashamed to stand before Lu'—modesty."
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to stand before Lu'—modesty."

sentences.zh: 開元中，說為集賢大學士十余年。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era Yue was Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies for over ten years.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era Yue was Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies for over ten years.

sentences.zh: 常與學士徐堅論近代文士，悲其雕喪。

translations.literal: He often with Academic Scholar Xu Jian discussed recent literary men, lamenting their ornate decline.
translations.idiomatic: He often with Academic Scholar Xu Jian discussed recent literary men, lamenting their ornate decline.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「李趙公、崔文公之筆術，擅價一時，其間孰優？」

translations.literal: Jian said: "Among the brushwork of Duke Li and Duke Cui, each monopolized price for a time—which was superior?"
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Among the brushwork of Duke Li and Duke Cui, each monopolized price for a time—which was superior?"

sentences.zh: 說曰：「李嶠、崔融、薛稷、宋之問之文，如良金美玉，無施不可。

translations.literal: Yue said: "The writing of Li Jiao, Cui Rong, Xue Ji, and Song Zhiwen is like fine gold and beautiful jade—there is no occasion where it cannot be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "The writing of Li Jiao, Cui Rong, Xue Ji, and Song Zhiwen is like fine gold and beautiful jade—there is no occasion where it cannot be applied.

sentences.zh: 富嘉謨之文，如孤峰絕岸，壁立萬仞，濃雲郁興，震雷俱發，誠可畏也，若施於廊廟，則駭矣！

translations.literal: Fu Jiamo's writing is like a lone peak and sheer cliff, standing ten thousand ren, dense clouds rising thick, thunderclaps all bursting forth—truly awesome; yet if applied in the court hall, it would alarm!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jiamo's writing is like a lone peak and sheer cliff, standing ten thousand ren, dense clouds rising thick, thunderclaps all bursting forth—truly awesome; yet if applied in the court hall, it would alarm!

sentences.zh: 閻朝隱之文，如麗服靚妝，燕歌趙舞，觀者忘疲，若類之風、雅，則罪人矣！」

translations.literal: Yan Chaoyin's writing is like fine clothes and splendid adornment, Yan songs and Zhao dances—the viewer forgets fatigue; yet if classed with the Airs and Elegances, it would be criminal!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Chaoyin's writing is like fine clothes and splendid adornment, Yan songs and Zhao dances—the viewer forgets fatigue; yet if classed with the Airs and Elegances, it would be criminal!"

sentences.zh: 問後進詞人之優劣，說曰：「韓休之文，如大羹旨酒，雅有典則，而薄於滋味。

translations.literal: Asked about the merits and defects of later poets, Yue said: "Han Xiu's writing is like great broth and fine wine—elegant with canonical norms, yet thin in flavor.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the merits and defects of later poets, Yue said, "Han Xiu's writing is like great broth and fine wine—elegant with canonical norms, yet thin in flavor.

sentences.zh: 許景先之文，如豐肌膩理，雖穠華可愛，而微少風骨。

translations.literal: Xu Jingxian's writing is like rich flesh and smooth texture—though lush and lovely, slightly lacking bone and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingxian's writing is like rich flesh and smooth texture—though lush and lovely, slightly lacking bone and spirit.

sentences.zh: 張九齡之文，如輕縑素練，實濟時用，而微窘邊幅。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling's writing is like light silk and plain silk—truly useful for the age, yet slightly cramped in breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling's writing is like light silk and plain silk—truly useful for the age, yet slightly cramped in breadth.

sentences.zh: 王翰之文，如瓊懷玉斝，雖爛然可珍，而多有玷缺。」

translations.literal: Wang Han's writing is like jade in the breast and jade cups—though brilliantly precious, often with many flaws."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han's writing is like jade in the breast and jade cups—though brilliantly precious, often with many flaws."

sentences.zh: 堅以為然。

translations.literal: Jian considered it so.
translations.idiomatic: Jian considered it so.

sentences.zh: 從父 德幹

translations.literal: Younger paternal uncle Degan
translations.idiomatic: Younger paternal uncle Degan

sentences.zh: 虔威子德幹，高宗末，歷澤、齊、汴、相四州刺史，治有威名，郡人為之語曰：「寧食三斗蒜，不逢楊德幹。」

translations.literal: Qianwei's son Degan, in the late Gaozong era served as Prefect of Ze, Qi, Bian, and Xiang—the four prefectures; his governance had awesomeness and fame; people of the commanderies said: "Better eat three pecks of garlic than meet Yang Degan."
translations.idiomatic: Qianwei's son Degan, in the late Gaozong era served as Prefect of Ze, Qi, Bian, and Xiang—the four prefectures; his governance had awesomeness and fame; people of the commanderies said, "Better eat three pecks of garlic than meet Yang Degan."

sentences.zh: 德幹子 神讓

translations.literal: Degan's son Shenrang
translations.idiomatic: Degan's son Shenrang

sentences.zh: 子神讓，天授初與徐敬業於揚州謀叛，父子伏誅。

translations.literal: Son Shenrang, in the early Tianshou era with Xu Jingye at Yang Prefecture plotted rebellion; father and son were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shenrang, in the early Tianshou era with Xu Jingye at Yang Prefecture plotted rebellion; father and son were executed.

sentences.zh: 王勃

translations.literal: Wang Bo
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo

sentences.zh: 王勃。

translations.literal: Wang Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo.

sentences.zh: 字子安，絳州龍門人。

translations.literal: Styled Zi'an, he was a man of Longmen in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Styled Zi'an, he was a man of Longmen in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖通，隋蜀郡司戶書佐。

translations.literal: Grandfather Tong, Records Clerk of the Household of Shu Commandery of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Tong, Records Clerk of the Household of Shu Commandery of Sui.

sentences.zh: 大業末，棄官歸，以著書講學為業。

translations.literal: In the late Daye era he abandoned office and returned home, making authorship and lecturing his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Daye era he abandoned office and returned home, making authorship and lecturing his occupation.

sentences.zh: 依《春秋》體例，自獲麟後，歷秦、漢至於後魏，著紀年之書，謂之《元經》。

translations.literal: Following the Spring and Autumn format, from after the Capture of the Lin stag through Qin and Han down to Later Wei he authored a chronicle book called the Original Classic.
